posts.excerpt: The step-by-step plan top agents use to launch a high-end listing, from positioning and cinematic video to paid ads and the first 14 days on market.
posts.html:
Luxury real estate marketing is the work of making a small, demanding pool of buyers feel something about a home before they ever visit. The best plans in 2026 combine sharp positioning, cinematic video, vertical social content, targeted paid ads and a tightly run launch window.

This playbook walks through each piece in the order you would actually do it, so you can use it for your next listing.

Key takeaways

  • Buyers of high-end homes are few and busy, so every asset has to earn attention in seconds.
  • Position the home around a lifestyle, not a list of features.
  • Cinematic video and vertical reels now do the heavy lifting on social media and in ads.
  • The first 14 days on market matter most. Plan the launch like a premiere.
  • Measure inquiries and showing requests, not likes.

What makes luxury real estate marketing different?

Luxury marketing is different because the buyer pool is tiny and the decision is emotional. A $5M buyer is not comparing 40 homes on a portal. They are deciding whether a property fits the life they want, and they expect the marketing to show it.

That changes three things:

  • Quality bar. Average photos and a slideshow signal an average home. Presentation is part of the product.
  • Reach. Many luxury buyers relocate or buy second homes, so your audience is spread across cities and countries.
  • Patience. Higher price points often take longer to sell, which means your content needs to stay fresh over weeks, not days.

How do you position a luxury listing?

Positioning is the one sentence that tells buyers who the home is for and why it is rare. Write it before you shoot a single photo, because every caption, ad and video script will follow from it.

A simple formula works well: For [buyer], this is the only home that [rare quality], so you can [lifestyle outcome].

For example: "For a family moving from New York, this is the only bayfront home on the street with a private dock and a garden-level guest suite, so weekends start the moment you get home."

Ask the sellers what they will miss most. Their answer is often the emotional center of the whole campaign.

Which marketing assets does a luxury listing need?

A luxury listing needs a core kit that works across the MLS, social media, email and ads. Build it once and reuse it everywhere.

Asset Why it matters Where it runs
Professional photography The foundation of every other asset MLS, portals, brochure
Cinematic listing video Sells the feeling and stops the scroll Instagram, TikTok, Facebook ads, YouTube
Vertical reels (15 to 30 seconds) Native format for social platforms Reels, TikTok, Stories
Property website or landing page One link that holds everything Ads, email, QR codes
Printed brochure Leave-behind for showings Showings, broker opens
Email announcement Reaches your sphere and broker network Email

If you only upgrade one thing, upgrade video. It is the asset buyers share, and it powers both organic posts and paid campaigns. Our guide to luxury real estate video marketing goes deeper on what a strong listing video includes.

How should you use video to market a luxury home?

Use video to show how life feels in the home, not just how the rooms connect. A walkthrough answers "what does it look like?" A cinematic video answers "what would my life be like here?", which is the question luxury buyers are really asking.

Strong luxury listing videos usually share a few traits:

  • A clear opening shot in the first two seconds, because viewers decide fast.
  • Moments of life: coffee on the terrace, friends at the island, a swim at dusk.
  • Original music and a voiceover that tells a short story.
  • Captions, since many people watch with the sound off.
  • A vertical version for social media, plus horizontal for the property website and YouTube.

You no longer need a shoot day to get there. AI-assisted cinematic video can be created from your existing listing photos, which keeps the home truthful while adding movement, light and atmosphere.

What is the best launch plan for a luxury listing?

The best launch plan treats the first two weeks like a premiere: build anticipation, go live everywhere at once, then keep momentum with fresh content. Here is a simple 14-day framework.

  1. Days -7 to -1, the teaser. Share a short "coming soon" reel with your sphere and broker network. Collect early interest.
  2. Day 0, the premiere. Publish the listing, the full cinematic video, the property page and the email announcement on the same day.
  3. Days 1 to 3, paid reach. Start a video ad campaign aimed at the buyer profile you defined in your positioning.
  4. Days 4 to 7, depth. Post room-by-room or lifestyle cutdowns, and a neighborhood reel.
  5. Days 8 to 14, proof. Share showing activity, a broker open recap or a short seller story.

Our step-by-step guide to Facebook ads for luxury listings covers the paid part in detail.

How do you market a luxury home on social media?

Market luxury homes on social media with vertical video first, then carousels and stories. Platforms like Instagram, TikTok and Facebook reward native vertical video, and short reels are the easiest content to share.

Post a mix of:

  • The hero reel of the property.
  • Lifestyle moments and neighborhood highlights.
  • Behind-the-scenes from preparing the listing.
  • Your point of view on the local luxury market.

Need ideas? Here are 15 Instagram Reels ideas for luxury realtors.

How do you measure luxury marketing results?

Measure luxury marketing by the actions that lead to a sale: inquiries, showing requests, video completion rates and the quality of leads. Likes and follower counts are nice, but they do not sell homes.

Track these for every listing:

  • Inquiries per week, by source.
  • Showing requests and broker interest.
  • Video views and how much of the video people watch.
  • Cost per qualified lead on paid campaigns.
  • Days on market compared with similar listings.

In our own case studies, realtors who ran cinematic videos as Facebook ad campaigns closed their listings about twice as fast. Every market is different, so set your own baseline and compare each listing against it.

How does great marketing help you win more listings?

Great marketing wins listings because sellers hire the agent who can show them how their home will be presented. Bring examples of cinematic videos to your listing presentation, and you are no longer competing on commission alone.

We break this down in our guide to the luxury listing presentation, and in how to build a luxury realtor personal brand.

Frequently asked questions

How much should you spend marketing a luxury listing?

There is no fixed rule. Many agents budget a set amount per listing and scale it with the price point and time on market. What matters most is that the budget covers strong photos, video and a paid campaign during the launch window.

Do luxury listings need video?

Video is not required, but it has become an expected part of high-end marketing. It shows how a home feels, works on every social platform and powers paid ads that reach buyers outside your local market.

How long does it take to sell a luxury home?

It depends on the market, price and condition. Higher price points often take longer because there are fewer buyers. Strong launch marketing helps you make the most of the first weeks, when interest is highest.

What is the most important part of a luxury marketing plan?

Positioning. If you know exactly who the home is for and why it is rare, every photo, video, caption and ad becomes sharper and more persuasive.

posts.meta: What makes a luxury listing video sell: story, pacing, music, voiceover and captions. A practical guide to luxury real estate video marketing for agents.
posts.excerpt: Why the best luxury listing videos feel like a story rather than a tour, and the exact ingredients that make high-end buyers stop scrolling.
posts.html:
Luxury real estate video marketing works when the video sells a feeling, not a floor plan. The listing videos that perform best for high-end homes tell a short story, open with a striking shot, use original music and voiceover, include captions for silent viewing and come in a vertical format for social media.

Below is what to include, what to skip and how to use the video once it is made.

Key takeaways

  • Luxury buyers are buying a lifestyle. Your video should show that life.
  • The first two seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching.
  • Captions matter because many viewers watch on mute.
  • Make vertical (9:16) the master format, then add horizontal and square versions.
  • One video can power the MLS, social posts, email and paid ads.

Why does video matter so much for luxury listings?

Video matters because it is the only format that shows how a home feels to live in. Photos show rooms. Video shows light moving across the terrace, the walk from the kitchen to the pool and the view at sunset, which is what luxury buyers are paying for.

It also travels. A strong video gets shared in group chats, reposted by brokers and used in ads that reach buyers who are relocating from other cities.

What is the difference between a walkthrough and a cinematic listing video?

A walkthrough moves through the home room by room. A cinematic listing video builds a short story around the people who might live there. Both have a place, but they do different jobs.

Walkthrough video Cinematic listing video
Goal Show the layout Create desire
Structure Room after room A short story with a beginning and end
Sound Stock music Original music and voiceover
Best for Serious buyers doing research Social media, ads and first impressions
Typical length 1 to 3 minutes 30 to 90 seconds

For high-end listings, the cinematic version usually earns more attention, because it gives viewers a reason to care before they get into the details.

What should a luxury listing video include?

A luxury listing video should include a strong opening shot, moments of real life, original music, a short voiceover, captions and clear text on screen with the address or price. Here is the checklist we use.

  1. A hook in the first two seconds. The most striking view, not the front door.
  2. A story arc. Morning to evening works beautifully: coffee at sunrise, a family lunch, a quiet swim as the lights come on.
  3. People, used carefully. Actors or lifestyle moments help buyers picture themselves in the home.
  4. Original music. It sets the mood and avoids the "stock track" feel buyers have heard a hundred times.
  5. Voiceover storytelling. Two or three short lines that name the feeling the home creates.
  6. Captions. Word-synced captions keep silent viewers watching.
  7. Text on screen. Address, price, key features and your brand.
  8. A clear ending. Your name, brokerage and how to book a showing.

How long should a luxury real estate video be?

For social media, aim for 30 to 60 seconds. For a property website or YouTube, a 60 to 90 second version gives serious buyers more depth. Short versions get watched to the end, which helps both the viewer and the platform.

A good approach is one master video with cutdowns: a 30-second reel for Instagram and TikTok, a 15-second teaser for stories and ads and a longer version for the listing page.

Which video format works best: vertical, horizontal or square?

Vertical (9:16) works best for Instagram Reels, TikTok and Stories, which is where most luxury buyers now discover content. Horizontal (16:9) suits YouTube and property websites. Square (1:1) still works in some Facebook and Instagram feed placements.

Make vertical your master. It is the format people watch on their phones, and it is the one ads platforms favor for short video.

Can you make a luxury listing video without a shoot day?

Yes. AI-assisted cinematic video can now be created from your existing listing photos, adding camera movement, light and atmosphere without sending a crew to the home. That means no scheduling around the sellers and delivery in days instead of weeks.

The key is staying truthful. Every scene should match the real photo it came from, with no invented windows, finishes or rooms. We explain how to do this safely in AI listing videos and MLS rules.

Where should you use your listing video?

Use your listing video everywhere the buyer might see it: the MLS (where allowed), your property page, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, email and paid ads. One strong video can support the whole campaign.

A simple rollout:

  • Day 0: full video on the property page and social channels.
  • Days 1 to 14: paid campaign using the 15 and 30-second cuts.
  • Weekly: a fresh cutdown or lifestyle moment to keep the listing visible.

For the full launch plan, see our complete luxury listing marketing playbook.

How do you measure whether a listing video worked?

Look at completion rate, inquiries and showing requests. If people watch most of the video and then ask about the home, it is working. If they drop off in the first few seconds, the opening needs work.

In our case studies, realtors who ran cinematic videos as Facebook ad campaigns closed listings about twice as fast. Treat that as a reason to test, then compare against your own past listings.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a luxury listing video cost?

It ranges widely. Traditional videographers often charge several hundred to over a thousand dollars per listing, and slideshow apps cost very little but look basic. We compare the options in our listing video cost comparison.

Should a luxury listing video have music?

Yes. Music sets the emotional tone. Original music also avoids the repetitive stock tracks buyers recognize and makes the video safer to use in paid ads.

Do I need to appear in my listing videos?

No. The home is the star. Many agents add a short branded ending with their name and contact details instead.

What is the best time to post a listing video?

Post it on launch day alongside the listing, then keep it in rotation with shorter cutdowns. Consistency over the first two weeks matters more than the exact hour you post.

The right choice depends on the listing, your timeline and how much the video needs to sell the feeling of the home.

  • Videographers deliver real footage but need a shoot day and often charge extra for scripts, voiceover and revisions.
  • Cinematic AI video uses your listing photos, so there is no shoot day, and delivery takes about 48 hours.

When is a videographer the right choice?

A videographer is the right choice when you need real footage that photos cannot capture, such as drone flights over a large estate, a walk-and-talk with the agent or interviews with the sellers. It is the most hands-on option.

The trade-offs are scheduling, time and add-ons. A shoot needs the home staged and the sellers out, weather can delay it and editing takes days. Scripts, voiceover and extra revisions often cost more.

When is a slideshow app enough?

A slideshow app is enough for entry-level listings where speed and cost matter more than polish. It turns photos into a moving sequence with stock music in minutes.

For luxury homes, slideshows tend to undersell the property. High-end buyers have seen the same pan-and-zoom effect for years, and it signals an average marketing budget for a home that is anything but average.

Cinematic AI video uses your existing listing photos as the foundation and creates movement, light and atmosphere around them with the latest AI models. Filmmakers direct each scene, write the script and add original music, voiceover and captions.

What should a listing video include, whatever the price?

Whatever you pay, make sure the video includes:

  • A strong opening shot in the first two seconds.
  • A vertical version for Reels and TikTok.
  • Captions for silent viewing.
  • Text on screen with the address, price and your brand.

posts.excerpt: Fifteen reel ideas, each with a ready-to-use hook, built to attract luxury buyers and the sellers who hire agents with great marketing.
posts.html:
The best Instagram Reels ideas for luxury realtors show lifestyle, not just square footage. Think cinematic listing reels, a day in the neighborhood, before-and-after staging, market updates in under 30 seconds and the stories behind special homes.

Here are 15 ideas, each with a hook line you can use or adapt.

Key takeaways

  • Open every reel with a striking visual or a strong line in the first two seconds.
  • Mix listing content with neighborhood, market and personal-brand reels.
  • Add captions, since many people watch without sound.
  • Your reels are also your portfolio. Sellers watch them before they call you.

Why should luxury realtors post Instagram Reels?

Reels are the format Instagram pushes to people who do not follow you yet, which makes them one of the best free ways to reach new buyers and sellers. For luxury agents, they double as a public portfolio that shows sellers how you present homes.

What are the best listing reels for luxury homes?

The best listing reels feel cinematic: a strong first shot, a sense of daily life and a clear ending with how to book a showing.

1. The cinematic hero reel. A 30-second story of a day in the home, from sunrise coffee to an evening swim. Hook: "This is what a Tuesday looks like at [address]."

2. The one-detail reel. Focus on a single feature that makes the home rare, like a wine room or a private dock. Hook: "There is one room in this house nobody expects."

3. The view reveal. Start inside, then open the doors to the view. Hook: "Wait for it."

4. The "coming soon" teaser. Short, mysterious, with no address. Hook: "Something special is coming to [neighborhood] next week."

5. Price-point comparison. "What $3M buys you in three neighborhoods." Great for reach and saves. Hook: "Here's what $3 million gets you in [city] right now."

Which neighborhood and lifestyle reels attract luxury buyers?

Neighborhood reels attract buyers who are relocating and want to understand the area before they look at homes. They also rank in Instagram search for place names.

6. A perfect Saturday in [neighborhood]. Coffee, beach or park, lunch, sunset spot. Hook: "If you're moving to [area], start here."

7. Hidden gems. Three places only locals know. Hook: "Three spots in [area] you won't find on a map."

8. Commute and convenience. Drive time to the airport, schools and downtown. Hook: "How far is everything from [neighborhood]? I timed it."

9. Waterfront vs. city living. A side-by-side of two lifestyles. Hook: "Bayfront or high-rise? Here's the honest difference."

Which reels build authority with luxury sellers?

Authority reels show sellers you understand the market and know how to present a high-end home. These are the reels that win listing appointments.

10. The 30-second market update. One number, one insight, one takeaway. Our luxury market report is a good source of ideas. Hook: "Luxury prices did something surprising this quarter."

11. How I prepare a luxury listing. Staging, photography and video, step by step. Hook: "Here's everything I do before a home hits the market."

12. Before and after. Staging or styling transformations. Hook: "Same room. One week apart."

13. Myth vs. fact. Clear up a common belief about selling a luxury home. Hook: "Pricing high to leave room to negotiate? Here's what actually happens."

Which personal brand reels work for luxury agents?

Personal brand reels help people trust you before they meet you. Keep them polished but human.

14. A day in my life. Showings, a broker open, a closing. Hook: "What a $10M listing week actually looks like."

15. Client story. With permission, share how you sold a special home. Hook: "This home sat for 9 months. We sold it in 3 weeks. Here's what changed."

Only use real numbers from your own sales. For more on building your brand, read how to build a luxury realtor personal brand.

How often should luxury realtors post reels?

Consistency beats volume. Three to four quality reels a week is a realistic rhythm for most agents, with a burst of listing content during each launch. A batch of cinematic listing reels makes that rhythm much easier to keep.

What makes a luxury reel look premium?

A premium reel has steady, smooth movement, natural light, restrained text, original or well-chosen music and captions in a clean font. Avoid busy transitions, loud stickers and trending audio that does not fit the home.

Do Avoid
Smooth, slow camera movement Fast zooms and spins
Clean captions, one font Multiple fonts and stickers
Music that matches the mood Trending audio that fights the visuals
A clear ending with your name No call to action

Frequently asked questions

How long should a real estate reel be?

Between 15 and 30 seconds works for most listing and market reels. Longer reels can work for storytelling, but only if the first seconds hook the viewer.

Should I use trending audio on luxury reels?

Use it sparingly. Trending audio can boost reach, but it often clashes with a high-end brand. Original music usually fits luxury listings better and is safer for ads.

Can I post the same reel on TikTok and Facebook?

Yes. Vertical reels work on TikTok, Facebook Reels and YouTube Shorts. Remove watermarks from other apps before reposting.

Do reels actually help sell luxury homes?

Reels help listings reach buyers and help agents win listings by showcasing their marketing. Pair them with a paid campaign for the strongest results. See our Facebook ads guide for luxury listings.

posts.meta: How to build a luxury listing presentation that wins high-end sellers: structure, pricing talk, marketing proof and the one asset that sets you apart.
posts.excerpt: A seven-part structure for listing appointments with luxury sellers, plus the marketing proof that makes them choose you over the agent who cut commission.
posts.html:
A winning luxury listing presentation shows sellers exactly how their home will be positioned, marketed and sold, with proof. The agents who win high-end listings arrive with a clear pricing story, a launch plan, real examples of their marketing and a preview of how the seller's own home could look on screen.

Here is a structure you can adapt for your next appointment.

Key takeaways

  • Luxury sellers hire for marketing confidence, not just price or commission.
  • Lead with listening. Ask what makes the home special to them.
  • Show, don't tell: bring real videos, reels and launch results.
  • A short preview video of their own home is a powerful differentiator.
  • End with a clear 14-day launch plan.

What do luxury sellers want from a listing agent?

Luxury sellers want an agent who understands what makes their home rare, can reach the right buyers wherever they are and will present the property at the level it deserves. Price and commission matter, but confidence in the marketing often decides the listing.

Many high-end sellers have bought and sold before. They have seen average marketing and know the difference.

How should you structure a luxury listing presentation?

Structure it as a conversation in seven parts: listen, position, price, market, launch, prove and agree. Keep slides minimal and let your examples do the work.

  1. Listen. Ask what they love about the home and what they will miss. Their words become your campaign.
  2. Position. Share the one-sentence story of who the home is for. Use the formula from our luxury marketing playbook.
  3. Price. Walk through comparable sales and your pricing logic. See how to value a luxury home.
  4. Market. Show the asset kit: photos, cinematic video, reels, property page, ads.
  5. Launch. Present a day-by-day plan for the first 14 days.
  6. Prove. Share past listing videos, reach and results from your own sales.
  7. Agree. Confirm next steps: photos, video, launch date.

How do you talk about price with luxury sellers?

posts.excerpt: How to set up Meta ads for a high-end listing, from housing ad rules to the video creative and retargeting that bring qualified buyers.
posts.html:
Facebook ads for luxury listings work best with a short cinematic video, a clear landing page and a campaign set up in Meta's housing Special Ad Category. Run the campaign during the first two weeks on market, retarget people who watched the video and measure inquiries, not clicks.

This guide walks through each step for Facebook and Instagram, which run on the same Meta ads platform.

Key takeaways

  • Real estate ads must use Meta's housing Special Ad Category, which limits targeting by age, gender and ZIP code.
  • Because targeting is limited, your creative does the targeting. Strong video attracts the right buyers.
  • Use a vertical 15 to 30-second video as the main ad.
  • Retarget people who watched most of the video or visited the property page.
  • Judge results by inquiries and showing requests.

Can you run Facebook ads for real estate listings?

Yes, but housing ads must run under Meta's Special Ad Category for housing. This exists to support fair housing, so it restricts targeting options such as age, gender and detailed location targeting. Always follow fair housing laws and Meta's current advertising policies.

The practical effect is that you cannot narrowly target "wealthy buyers." Instead, the ad itself must attract them, which is why the creative matters so much for luxury.

What kind of ad creative works for luxury listings?

Short, cinematic vertical video works best. It stops the scroll, shows how the home feels and naturally attracts people who are drawn to that lifestyle. A good luxury ad has a striking first shot, captions, a short line of copy and one clear action.

Element What works
Format Vertical 9:16 video, 15 to 30 seconds
Opening The best view or most unusual feature in the first two seconds
Sound Original music and voiceover, with captions
Copy One or two lines about the lifestyle, then price or address
Call to action "Learn more" or "Book a private showing"

Our guide to luxury real estate video marketing explains how to build the video itself.

How do you set up a luxury listing campaign step by step?

  1. Choose the objective. For new listings, choose a traffic or leads objective. For awareness of a teaser, video views can work.
  2. Select the housing Special Ad Category. This is required for real estate.
  3. Set your location. Target the metro area and, if your buyers often relocate, the cities they come from.
  4. Add your creative. Upload the vertical video plus a square or horizontal version for other placements.
  5. Write short copy. Lead with the feeling, then the facts.
  6. Send traffic to one page. A property page with the video, photos and a simple inquiry form.
  7. Set a launch budget. Spend more in the first 14 days, when interest is highest.
  8. Set up retargeting. Build audiences of people who watched most of the video or visited the page.

Need ad-ready video? Every Wonder Ads cinematic video is built to perform in Facebook and Instagram campaigns, with original music you can use in paid ads. Create My Free Video.

How much should you spend on Facebook ads for a luxury listing?

There is no single right number. Many agents set a fixed launch budget per listing and spend most of it in the first two weeks, then keep a smaller retargeting budget running until the home sells. Start with an amount you are comfortable testing and adjust based on the cost per qualified inquiry.

How does retargeting help sell luxury homes?

Retargeting shows follow-up ads to people who already showed interest, such as watching most of your video or visiting the property page. These viewers are far more likely to inquire, and luxury buyers often need several touches before they reach out.

Good retargeting ads include a different scene from the home, a neighborhood reel or an invitation to a private showing.

What should you measure in a luxury ad campaign?

Measure the actions that lead to a sale:

  • Video completion rate (how much of the video people watch).
  • Landing page visits and time on page.
  • Inquiries and showing requests.
  • Cost per qualified inquiry.
  • Days on market compared with similar listings.

In our case studies, realtors who ran cinematic videos as Facebook ad campaigns closed listings about twice as fast. Your results will depend on your market and price point, so compare each campaign with your own past listings.

What are common mistakes with luxury real estate ads?

  • Boosting a photo post. A single photo rarely shows what makes a luxury home special.
  • Skipping the Special Ad Category. Ads can be rejected or disapproved.
  • Sending traffic to a busy portal page. Use a clean page focused on one home.
  • Stopping after a week. Luxury buyers move slowly. Keep retargeting running.
  • Writing feature lists. Lead with lifestyle, then facts.

Can Facebook ads help you win more listings too?

Yes. Running visible, high-quality ads shows sellers in your market that you invest in marketing. Mention your ad strategy in your listing presentation and show past campaign results.

Are Facebook ads effective for luxury real estate?

They can be, especially with strong video and retargeting. Meta's reach makes it possible to show a home to buyers in other cities who are planning a move.

It is a Meta setting required for housing ads. It limits certain targeting options to help prevent discrimination, in line with fair housing laws.

Should I run ads on Instagram too?

Yes. Facebook and Instagram ads run from the same Meta ads platform, and vertical video performs well in Instagram Reels and Stories placements.

How long should a luxury listing ad run?

Run the main campaign through the first two weeks, then keep retargeting active until the home is under contract. Refresh the creative every couple of weeks so it does not go stale.

posts.excerpt: AI can make listing videos stunning, but it can also invent rooms that don't exist. Here's how to keep every scene true to the home.
posts.html:
AI listing videos are safe to use when every scene stays true to the real home. That means no invented windows, finishes, views or rooms, clear disclosure where your MLS or brokerage requires it and a scene-by-scene check against the original photos before you publish.

Rules differ between MLSs and brokerages, so always check your own. This guide covers the principles that apply almost everywhere.

Key takeaways

  • Misrepresenting a property is a serious risk, whether a human or an AI made the mistake.
  • Build AI video from real listing photos, and check every scene against its source.
  • Detail-heavy rooms like kitchens and bathrooms need subtle, true-to-photo motion.
  • Keep virtual-staging disclosure labels where they exist.
  • Read your MLS and brokerage rules on enhanced media before publishing.

Can you use AI-generated video for real estate listings?

Yes, many agents now use AI-assisted video in their marketing. The question is not whether AI was used, but whether the result accurately represents the property. Buyers rely on listing media to make decisions, so anything that changes what the home actually has is a problem.

Some MLSs restrict video on the listing itself or have specific rules for virtually staged or enhanced media. Check yours before uploading, and use social media and your property page where MLS rules are stricter.

What can go wrong with AI listing videos?

AI video models are trained to make things look beautiful, and sometimes they fill gaps with details that are not there. Common errors include:

  • Extra windows or doors.
  • Different countertops, floors or fixtures.
  • A view that does not match the real one.
  • Rooms that are larger or shaped differently.
  • Furniture appearing or disappearing.

On social media, that is a glitch. On a listing, it can be misrepresentation.

How do you keep an AI listing video truthful?

Keep it truthful by starting from real photos, limiting how much the AI changes, reviewing every scene against the original and redoing anything that does not match. Here is the process we follow at Wonder Ads.

  1. Start from the real MLS photos. Every scene begins with a photo of the actual room.
  2. Use gentle motion in detail-heavy rooms. Kitchens, bathrooms and built-ins get subtle camera movement so the AI has less room to invent.
  3. Check side by side. Compare layout, fixtures, counters, windows and views with the source photo.
  4. Redo what doesn't match. Any scene with an invented detail is regenerated or removed.
  5. Keep disclosures. If a photo was virtually staged and labeled, the label stays in.
  6. Share the proof. Provide a scene-by-scene comparison the agent can show to their broker or seller.

MLS-safe by design. Every Wonder Ads video comes with a scene-by-scene comparison to your original photos, ready to share with your broker or seller. See how it works.

Do you have to disclose AI-enhanced listing media?

Disclosure rules vary. Many MLSs and brokerages already require labels on virtually staged photos, and some are adding guidance for AI-enhanced media. When in doubt, disclose. A short note such as "Video includes AI-enhanced motion created from listing photos" is easy and builds trust.

This is not legal advice. Your MLS rules, brokerage policy and local regulations decide what is required.

What about people in AI listing videos?

Adding people, such as a couple enjoying the terrace, can help buyers picture the lifestyle. It does not misrepresent the home as long as the property itself stays accurate. Keep casting and scenes consistent with fair housing guidelines, and avoid anything that suggests a preference for certain buyers.

Which rooms need the most care?

Room or feature Why it needs care Approach
Kitchens Many small details: hardware, appliances, counters Subtle motion, close check of fixtures
Bathrooms Tiles, fixtures, mirrors Minimal movement
Windows and views Easy for AI to add or change Compare window count and view
Exteriors Rooflines, landscaping, neighbors Check structure and surroundings
Floor plans and room size Wide-angle motion can distort space Avoid exaggerated movement

How do you explain AI video to sellers and brokers?

Explain it simply: the video is built from the real listing photos, adds camera movement and atmosphere and is checked scene by scene so nothing is invented. Then show the comparison sheet. Most sellers are excited, and brokers appreciate the documentation.

For more on using video in your marketing, read our luxury real estate video marketing guide and the listing video cost comparison.

Frequently asked questions

Is AI real estate video legal?

Using AI tools is generally fine. What matters is accuracy and following your MLS, brokerage and local advertising rules. Misrepresenting a property is the risk to avoid.

Can I upload an AI listing video to the MLS?

It depends on your MLS. Some allow branded or unbranded video links, some restrict enhanced media. Check the current rules or ask your MLS directly.

Does AI video replace professional photography?

No. Great AI video depends on great photos. See our luxury real estate photography checklist.

How do I know an AI video is accurate?

Ask for a scene-by-scene comparison with the original photos. If the provider cannot show one, review the video yourself before publishing.

A luxury realtor personal brand is the reputation sellers and buyers know you for before they meet you. The strongest brands in 2026 combine a clear niche, a consistent premium look, useful market content and visible proof of how you present homes, especially through video.

  • Your listing marketing is your best brand content.

Why does personal branding matter for luxury agents?

Branding matters because luxury sellers interview agents they already trust. Many choose based on reputation, referrals and what they have seen online. A strong brand gets you invited to the listing appointment, and your marketing examples help you win it.

How do you choose a luxury niche?

Choose a niche where you can become the obvious name. It can be geographic, like a waterfront neighborhood, or based on property type, like new-construction estates or penthouses. It can also be a buyer type, such as families relocating from the Northeast.

A simple test: can someone finish the sentence "If you're selling a [niche] home, call ___" with your name? If not, narrow it.

What should a luxury agent's visual identity look like?

Your visual identity should feel calm, consistent and confident. Use a simple logo or wordmark, one or two fonts, a restrained color palette and the same editing style for photos and video. Luxury branding usually means more space and fewer elements, not more decoration.

Post around three or four pillars so people know what to expect from you:

  1. Listings. Cinematic videos and reels of the homes you represent.

Testimonials help most when they are specific: "She had a video ready before the photos were even back" is stronger than "Great agent!"

Where should a luxury agent build their brand online?

Focus on two or three channels you can keep up with. For most luxury agents that means Instagram for visual content, a website with your listings and market insight and one more channel such as YouTube, LinkedIn or Facebook depending on where your sellers spend time.

Your website matters because it is the one channel you own. Market articles and neighborhood guides on your site can also bring search traffic over time.

How do you keep your brand consistent when you're busy?

Batch and systemize. Plan content monthly, film or collect assets in one session and use templates for captions and graphics. For listings, a repeatable video process keeps every launch on-brand without extra work.

How long does it take to build a luxury real estate brand?

Expect months, not weeks. Consistent posting and a steady stream of well-marketed listings build recognition over time. The good news: every listing you market well becomes brand content that keeps working.

Both help. Your brokerage brings credibility and reach, and your personal brand is why sellers choose you within it. Most luxury agents build a personal brand that works alongside their brokerage's identity.

Usually yes. People hire people, and seeing you helps them trust you. That said, your listings should let the home be the star.

Upgrade your listing presentation: better photos, cinematic video and a clean, consistent style. It is the content sellers judge you by.

posts.excerpt: The usual suspects behind a stale high-end listing, and how to relaunch it so buyers look again.
posts.html:
A luxury home usually stops selling for one of three reasons: the price is out of line with the market, the marketing doesn't show why the home is special or the home isn't reaching the right buyers. The fix is a relaunch: reset the price strategy, refresh the presentation with new photos and cinematic video and push it to buyers in and outside your market.

Here are nine fixes, in the order we would try them.

Key takeaways

  • Stale listings lose attention fast. Treat a relaunch as a new premiere.
  • Price and presentation work together. Fix both.
  • New video and photos give buyers a reason to look again.
  • Reach buyers who are relocating, not just local searchers.
  • Collect feedback from showings and use it.

Why do luxury homes sit on the market?

Luxury homes sit on the market because there are fewer buyers at higher price points, and those buyers are selective. When a home is overpriced, presented like an average listing or marketed only locally, it can quietly fall off buyers' radar.

Time on market also feeds on itself. The longer a listing sits, the more buyers wonder what is wrong with it.

Fix 1: Is the price right for today's market?

Review the price against recent comparable sales, active competition and buyer feedback. If the home has had showings but no offers, price is often part of the story. Our guide to how to value a luxury home explains why comps get tricky at the top of the market.

A price change works best when paired with fresh marketing, so buyers see a new listing rather than a discount.

Fix 2: Does the marketing show why the home is special?

If the photos and description could describe any home in the area, buyers have no reason to care. Rewrite the positioning around the one thing that makes the home rare, then rebuild the marketing around it.

Fix 3: Refresh the photos

Reshoot in better light, restyle key rooms and add twilight exteriors. Fresh images also reset how the listing appears in portals and social feeds.

Fix 4: Add a cinematic listing video

A cinematic video gives the listing a new first impression and a shareable asset for social media and ads. Show the lifestyle: mornings on the terrace, evenings by the pool. See our guide to luxury real estate video marketing.

Relaunch a stale listing in 48 hours. Wonder Ads turns your current photos into a cinematic reel video with original music and voiceover, no shoot day needed. Create My Free Video.

Fix 5: Run paid video ads

Paid ads put the home in front of buyers who are not actively searching portals, including people planning a move from another city. Use the vertical video as the main ad and retarget viewers. Our Facebook ads guide for luxury listings walks through setup.

Fix 6: Reach relocating and second-home buyers

Many luxury buyers come from outside the area. Share the listing with agents in the cities your buyers usually come from, and target ads to those markets.

Fix 7: Improve showings

Check the basics: lighting, temperature, scent, clutter and how easy it is to schedule. Provide a printed brochure and a QR code to the video so buyers can rewatch it later and share it with their partner.

Fix 8: Collect and act on feedback

Ask every showing agent for honest feedback, then group it into price, condition and presentation. If the same comment keeps coming up, address it directly.

Fix 9: Relaunch like it's new

Bundle the changes into a clear relaunch: new photos, new video, any price update and a fresh campaign, all going live on the same day. A coordinated relaunch gets more attention than small changes made one at a time.

Few showings Marketing or reach New video and paid ads
Showings, no offers Price or condition Price review and feedback
Lots of views, few inquiries Unclear story or weak call to action Repositioning and clearer next step

How do you talk to sellers about a stale listing?

Be direct and bring data. Show views, showings and feedback, then present the relaunch plan. Sellers usually respond well to a clear plan that combines a fresh presentation with a realistic price.

Frequently asked questions

How long is too long for a luxury home to be on the market?

It depends on the price point and local market. If showings and inquiries have slowed well below similar homes, it is time to review price and marketing rather than wait.

Should I take the listing off the market and relist it?

Some agents do this to reset days on market. Rules vary by MLS, so check yours. A real relaunch with new marketing matters more than the relisting itself.

Does a price reduction hurt a luxury listing?

A well-timed price change paired with fresh marketing can bring new buyers. Small, repeated reductions without new marketing tend to work less well.

A new video gives buyers a new reason to look and gives you fresh content for ads and social media. It works best as part of a full relaunch.

posts.excerpt: Luxury buyers aren't buying square footage, they're buying a life. Here's how to market that life, scene by scene.
posts.html:
Lifestyle marketing in luxury real estate means selling the life a home makes possible, not just its features. Instead of "5 bedrooms, 6 baths, pool," you show Sunday lunches on the terrace, kids racing to the dock and quiet evenings watching the skyline. It works because high-end buyers make emotional decisions and then justify them with facts.

Here is how to do it well.

Key takeaways

  • Buyers decide with emotion and confirm with facts. Give them both, in that order.
  • Find the "moments" a home creates and build the marketing around them.
  • Cinematic video with people is the most direct way to show lifestyle.
  • Write copy that describes experiences, then list the features.
  • Stay truthful. Lifestyle marketing should never misrepresent the property.

What is lifestyle marketing in real estate?

Lifestyle marketing is a way of presenting a property through the experiences it offers. It answers the buyer's real question, "What would my life be like here?", using story, imagery, video and copy that put the viewer inside the home.

Why does lifestyle marketing work for luxury homes?

It works because luxury buyers are rarely buying out of necessity. They are buying a better version of their life: more space for family, a place to entertain, a view to wake up to. When marketing shows that life, buyers connect with the home before they compare it.

How do you find a home's lifestyle story?

Find it by asking what moments the home was made for. Walk through it at different times of day, talk to the sellers and look for the places where life naturally happens.

Questions to ask the sellers:

  • Where do you spend most of your time?
  • What will you miss most?
  • What is your favorite time of day here, and why?
  • How do you use the home when friends visit?

Their answers often hold the campaign's central idea.

How do you show lifestyle in a listing video?

Show lifestyle by building the video around a short day in the life, with people in key moments. A sunrise coffee, a family lunch, a swim at dusk and lights coming on across the water make a simple, powerful arc.

We explain the full structure in our guide to luxury real estate video marketing, and offer copy-paste scripts in luxury listing video script templates.

We sell the lifestyle. You sell the property. Wonder Ads creates cinematic listing videos that show buyers the life a home offers, with actors, original music and voiceover. Create My Free Video.

How do you write lifestyle copy for a listing?

Lead with an experience, then support it with facts. Keep sentences short and specific, and avoid generic phrases like "entertainer's dream."

Feature-only copy Lifestyle copy
"Pool with outdoor kitchen." "Long lunches by the pool, with the grill steps away."
"Primary suite with bay views." "Wake up to the bay from bed."
"Private dock, 70 ft frontage." "Take the boat out before breakfast. The dock is yours."
"Open-plan kitchen with island." "Everyone ends up around the island, and there's room for them all."

Follow the lifestyle lines with the full specs, so serious buyers get the details they need.

Which channels are best for lifestyle marketing?

Vertical video channels like Instagram Reels and TikTok are ideal, because they reward emotional, visual storytelling. Paid ads extend that reach to buyers in other cities. Your property page and brochure should carry the same story so the experience feels consistent.

How do you keep lifestyle marketing truthful?

Keep the property itself accurate. People, light and mood are fair to show, but the home's features, views and rooms must match reality. Our guide to AI listing videos and MLS rules covers this in detail.

Also keep fair housing in mind. Show lifestyles and activities, and avoid language or imagery that suggests a preference for certain types of buyers.

Does lifestyle marketing work for every luxury home?

It works best for furnished, styled homes where every room already tells a story. Vacant homes can still use lifestyle marketing through staging, neighborhood scenes and views, but the story is stronger when the home feels lived in.

Frequently asked questions

Is lifestyle marketing only for luxury homes?

No, but it matters most at higher price points, where buyers have more choice and the decision is more emotional.

Should listing videos include people?

People help buyers picture themselves in the home. Use them for lifestyle moments, keep the focus on the property and keep scenes inclusive.

How do I find lifestyle content for a neighborhood?

Spend a day there. Film the coffee spot, the waterfront, the school run and sunset. Neighborhood reels are some of the most shared content agents make.

What's the biggest lifestyle marketing mistake?

Leading with a feature list. Facts matter, but they belong after the story has made the buyer care.

posts.html:
Luxury real estate photography needs more than wide shots of every room. A strong shoot covers the hero exterior, twilight, views, signature details, lifestyle spaces and the neighborhood, all in high resolution with natural light. Plan the shot list with video in mind, and the same photos can become a cinematic listing video.

Use this checklist for your next shoot.

Key takeaways

  • Prepare the home first. Styling matters more than equipment.
  • Shoot in the best natural light, plus a twilight session.
  • Capture details and lifestyle spaces, not just whole rooms.
  • Deliver high-resolution files with no watermarks.
  • Think in sequences. Photos that flow together make better video.

How do you prepare a luxury home for photos?

Prepare the home by decluttering, styling key surfaces and fixing small details before the photographer arrives. Clear counters, remove personal items, open blinds, turn on every light, straighten towels and pillows and set the outdoor furniture.

A quick prep list:

  • Hide cords, remotes, trash cans and toiletries.
  • Add fresh flowers or greenery in a few spots.
  • Make the beds with crisp, light linens.
  • Turn on pool and landscape lighting for twilight.
  • Move cars out of the driveway.

What shots does a luxury listing need?

A luxury listing needs a complete set that tells the story of the home from arrival to evening. Here is our must-have list.

Category Shots
Exterior Hero front, angled front, rear facade, aerial or high angle, entry and front door
Twilight Front at dusk, pool and terrace at dusk, view at dusk
Living spaces Great room wide, a second angle, dining, family room
Kitchen Wide, island detail, appliances, butler's pantry
Primary suite Bedroom wide, view from the bed, bath wide, closet
Other rooms Each bedroom, office, gym, wine room, theater
Outdoor living Pool, outdoor kitchen, terraces, garden, dock
Details Fixtures, materials, art niches, fireplace, staircase
Views From the main rooms and terraces
Neighborhood Waterfront, parks, nearby landmarks

How do you light luxury real estate photos?

Use natural light wherever possible, shoot each side of the home when the sun is soft and add a twilight session for exteriors and views. Twilight images often become the most memorable photos in the set.

Avoid heavy filters and over-brightened skies. Buyers notice when photos don't match the home in person.

What file specs work best for listing photos and video?

Ask your photographer for high-resolution JPEGs, no watermarks and consistent color editing. Landscape orientation is standard, but a few vertical shots of key spaces are useful for social media.

  • High resolution (full-size files, not web-compressed).
  • No watermarks or logos on the images.
  • Consistent white balance across the set.
  • A few vertical versions of hero spaces.
  • Clear file names by room.

How do you shoot photos that also work for video?

Shoot in sequences that follow how someone moves through the home: approach, entry, living space, kitchen, terrace, view. Include a few angles of each hero space and some close details. This gives video editors and AI tools natural "scenes" to work with.

When photos are going to become a cinematic video, every frame matters, because each scene is built from a real photo. We explain how scenes stay true to the photos in AI listing videos and MLS rules.

Do you need drone photography for luxury listings?

Drone photos help when location is part of the value: waterfront, golf course, large lots or skyline views. Always use a licensed operator and follow local airspace rules.

What are common luxury photography mistakes?

  • Shooting before the home is styled.
  • Only wide shots, no details.
  • Over-edited skies and colors.
  • Skipping twilight.
  • Missing the view from inside.
  • Delivering low-resolution or watermarked files.

Frequently asked questions

How many photos should a luxury listing have?

Enough to tell the full story, often 40 to 60 or more for large homes. Check your MLS photo limits and lead with the strongest images.

For luxury homes, usually yes. Twilight shots show lighting, pools and views at their best and are often the most shared images.

Yes. High-resolution photos can be turned into a cinematic listing video without a shoot day. See our listing video cost comparison.

posts.excerpt: Five fill-in-the-blank voiceover scripts for 30-second luxury listing videos, plus the rules that make a script sound natural.
posts.html:
A great real estate video script for a luxury listing is short, specific and emotional. For a 30-second video, aim for roughly 60 to 75 words: an opening line that sets a feeling, two or three lines about life in the home and a closing line with the address or a call to action.

Below are five templates you can copy and adapt.

Key takeaways

  • Keep 30-second scripts to about 60 to 75 words, read slowly.
  • Write for the ear: short sentences, natural pauses.
  • Describe moments and feelings, then add facts on screen.
  • Use one consistent, warm tone from start to finish.
  • End with a clear next step.

How long should a real estate video script be?

A 30-second video needs about 60 to 75 words if the voiceover leaves room for pauses and music. A 60-second video can carry roughly 120 to 150 words. Read it aloud with a timer, and cut until it breathes.

What makes a luxury listing script work?

It works when it sounds like a person talking, not a brochure. Lead with a feeling, name specific moments and let the visuals and on-screen text carry the specs.

Rules we follow:

  • One idea per sentence.
  • Specific images ("coffee on the terrace") over vague claims ("luxurious living").
  • A steady, warm tone. Avoid swinging from soft to hype.
  • Pauses between lines so the music can breathe.

Template 1: Waterfront home

Some mornings start with an alarm. Here, they start with the water. Coffee on the terrace. The boat waiting at the dock. Long lunches in the shade, and evenings that end with the city lights across the bay. [Home name], [neighborhood]. Life, closer to the water.

On screen: address, price, beds/baths, dock length.

Template 2: Penthouse

Above the city, everything slows down. Morning light fills every room. Dinner comes with a skyline view. And at night, the whole city sparkles just for you. [Building], residence [number]. The view is only the beginning.

On screen: floor, square footage, terrace size, price.

Template 3: Family estate

Every family has a place where the memories happen. Saturday breakfasts around the island. Cannonballs into the pool. Friends who stay a little longer, because there's room for everyone. [Address]. A home made for the moments that matter.

On screen: bedrooms, lot size, schools nearby, price.

Prefer not to write it yourself? Every Wonder Ads video includes a concept, script and voiceover in a warm, energetic or focused style, or you can send your own script with a custom order. Build a Custom Order.

Template 4: New construction

Designed for the way we live now. Clean lines. Natural light. Every detail chosen with care. Room to work, room to gather and room to simply breathe. [Project name], [neighborhood]. Brand new, and ready for your story.

On screen: builder, completion date, specs, price.

Template 5: Coming-soon teaser (15 seconds)

Something special is coming to [neighborhood]. A home with a view you'll want to wake up to. Coming soon. Follow for the premiere.

On screen: "Coming soon" and your name.

How do you choose the right voiceover tone?

Match the tone to the home and buyer. Waterfront and family homes suit a warm tone. New construction and penthouses can take a cleaner, more focused delivery. Energetic delivery works for younger buyers and investment properties. Whatever you choose, keep it consistent throughout.

Tone Best for
Warm Family estates, waterfront, legacy homes
Focused Penthouses, new construction, design-led homes
Energetic Investment properties, younger buyers, social teasers

Should every listing video have a voiceover?

A voiceover makes the video feel like a story, and captions let silent viewers follow along. Some agents prefer music only, which can work for short teasers. For a hero video, a short voiceover usually connects more strongly with buyers.

Learn how the script fits into the whole video in our luxury real estate video marketing guide and our article on lifestyle marketing.

Frequently asked questions

How many words is a 30-second script?

About 60 to 75 words for a relaxed pace with pauses. Faster delivery can fit more, but luxury videos usually benefit from a slower rhythm.

Should I mention the price in the voiceover?

Usually put the price on screen instead. It keeps the voiceover focused on the feeling while still giving buyers the facts.

Can I use AI voices for listing videos?

Yes, many agents do. Choose a natural, warm voice and keep the pacing slow so it sounds human.

Who should read the voiceover?

A professional voice, an AI voice or you. If you voice it yourself, record in a quiet room and read slowly.

posts.html:
The U.S. luxury real estate market is still rising in 2026, but unevenly. According to Redfin, the median luxury home sold for about $1.39 million in the three months ending April 2026, up 3.6% from a year earlier, with pending luxury sales up 4.3%. Gains are strongest in Sun Belt metros like Tampa and Las Vegas, while New York and Denver saw small declines.

Here is what the latest data shows and what it means if you list or sell high-end homes. Figures reflect the latest reports available at the time of writing. We update this page as new data comes out.

Key takeaways

  • The U.S. median luxury sale price was about $1.39 million, up 3.6% year over year (Redfin, three months ending April 2026).
  • Luxury pending sales rose 4.3%, new listings rose 2.0% and active listings rose 1.4%.
  • Tampa (+17.1%), Las Vegas (+16.1%) and Kansas City (+15.2%) led luxury price growth.
  • South Florida's high-end sales jumped in Q2 2026, led by Miami-Dade single-family homes.
  • The typical luxury home now costs 3.6 times a typical non-luxury home, up from 3.5.

How is the luxury real estate market doing in 2026?

The luxury market is growing steadily rather than booming. Redfin defines luxury homes as the top 5% of each metro by estimated value. In the three months ending April 2026, their median sale price rose 3.6% to about $1.39 million, and pending luxury sales rose 4.3% year over year.

Supply is loosening slowly. Luxury new listings rose 2.0% and active luxury listings rose 1.4%, a smaller increase than in the non-luxury market (2.3%).

Measure (U.S., luxury homes) Change vs. a year earlier
Median sale price (about $1.39M) +3.6%
Pending sales +4.3%
New listings +2.0%
Active listings +1.4%

Source: Redfin, three months ending April 30, 2026.

Where are luxury home prices rising fastest?

Luxury prices rose most in Tampa (17.1%), Las Vegas (16.1%) and Kansas City (15.2%) over the same period, according to Redfin. Prices fell in only four major metros: Detroit (-2.4%), Cincinnati (-1.6%), New York (-0.6%) and Denver (-0.6%).

For agents, the takeaway is local. National averages hide big differences between markets, so your pricing and marketing should reflect what is happening in your metro.

Is the gap between luxury and regular homes growing?

Yes. Redfin reported in July 2026 that the typical luxury home costs 3.6 times as much as a typical non-luxury home, up from 3.5 a year earlier. The widest gaps were in West Palm Beach (8.9 times) and Miami (8.8 times, up from 7.6), followed by New York, Los Angeles and Phoenix.

We break down the most expensive metros in our guide to the most expensive luxury housing markets in the U.S.

What is happening in South Florida's luxury market?

South Florida is one of the strongest luxury regions in the country right now. The Keyes Company and Illustrated Properties' Q2 2026 Luxury Market Report found that high-end single-family sales across its five-county region rose 20.1% to 8,013, with the average price up 7.2% to $2.63 million.

Miami-Dade stood out: luxury single-family transactions rose 32.5% to 1,000 and the average price jumped 21.9% to $3.61 million. Read more in our Miami luxury real estate market report and our Palm Beach vs. Miami comparison.

More buyers are active. Make sure they see your listing first. Wonder Ads creates cinematic listing videos built for social media and paid ads, delivered in 48 hours. Create My Free Video.

How does the U.S. compare with global prime markets?

Globally, prime prices are rising modestly. Knight Frank's Prime Global Cities Index showed average annual growth of 2.6% in Q2 2026. Among U.S. cities in the index, San Francisco rose 5.0%, Miami 3.9% and Los Angeles 1.4%, while New York slipped 0.4%. Tokyo led the world with 50.7%.

See our full breakdown of where the world's wealthy are buying in 2026.

What do these trends mean for luxury agents?

They mean buyers are active, but they are selective and spread across markets. Three practical moves:

  1. Price from local data, not national headlines. A 17% gain in Tampa says little about New York.
  2. Market to relocating buyers. Strong demand in the Sun Belt and Florida often comes from out of state.
  3. Win attention fast. With more listings coming to market, presentation and launch speed matter more.

Our complete luxury listing marketing playbook covers how to do all three.

What should luxury sellers know in 2026?

Sellers should know that demand is healthy in many markets, but buyers have more choice than a year ago as listings slowly rise. Homes that are well priced and beautifully presented tend to stand out. Homes that are overpriced can sit, as we explain in why luxury homes don't sell.

What is the average price of a luxury home in the U.S.?

Redfin put the median U.S. luxury home sale price at about $1.39 million in the three months ending April 2026. Luxury thresholds vary widely by metro. See what is considered a luxury home.

Is the luxury housing market slowing down?

Not overall. Prices and pending sales were both up year over year in Redfin's latest data, though a few metros, including New York and Denver, saw small price declines.

Which U.S. cities have the hottest luxury markets?

By luxury price growth, Tampa, Las Vegas and Kansas City led in Redfin's latest report. By sales activity, South Florida markets like Miami-Dade posted strong gains in Q2 2026.

Will luxury home prices go up in 2027?

No one can say for certain. Prices depend on interest rates, the stock market, migration and local supply. Watch local data and quarterly reports, and plan for different scenarios.

According to Redfin's data for the three months ending May 2026, Miami's median luxury home was about $4.86 million, the highest of the metros in its report.

Here is the full picture, including where the gap between luxury and regular homes is widest.

Key takeaways

  • Miami had the highest median luxury price in Redfin's report at about $4.86 million.
  • Los Angeles (about $4.51M), West Palm Beach (about $4.51M) and New York (about $4.38M) followed.
  • West Palm Beach and Miami have the widest luxury premiums, close to 9 times a typical home.
  • Miami's premium jumped the most in a year, from 7.6 to 8.8 times.

Which U.S. metros have the most expensive luxury homes?

Luxury = top 5% of homes in each metro by estimated value. Non-luxury = 35th to 65th percentile. Source: Redfin.

What is the "luxury premium," and why does it matter?

The luxury premium is how many times more a typical luxury home costs than a typical mid-market home in the same metro. Nationally, it was 3.6 times in Redfin's latest data, up from 3.5 a year earlier.

A high premium means the top of the market is pulling away from everyone else. In West Palm Beach and Miami, luxury homes cost almost nine times what a typical home does, which reflects both wealthy buyers moving in and the scarcity of prime waterfront property.

Where is the luxury premium growing fastest?

Miami's premium grew the most, from 7.6 to 8.8 times in a year. Tampa (3.8 to 4.4), Phoenix (4.3 to 4.8) and Nashville and Philadelphia (each up 0.2 to 4.6) also saw notable increases, according to Redfin.

Florida appears twice in that list, which lines up with strong luxury sales activity in the state. See our Miami luxury market report for more.

Where is luxury real estate most affordable?

Among major metros, the smallest luxury premiums were in Portland, Oregon (2.6 times, with a median luxury price of about $1.46 million), Columbus, Ohio (2.9 times, about $1.02 million) and Sacramento (3.0 times, about $1.72 million). Mostly, but not everywhere. Redfin's May 2026 report showed luxury prices falling slightly in New York (-0.6%), while Florida and Sun Belt markets kept climbing. Read our 2026 luxury market report for the national view.

A strong flow of wealthy buyers, limited waterfront land and a wide gap between prime and typical homes all contribute. Miami's premium rose from 7.6 to 8.8 times in a year.

Yes. New York's median luxury price was about $4.38 million, among the highest in the country, even though luxury prices dipped slightly year over year.

Key takeaways

  • Miami-Dade luxury single-family sales rose 32.5% to 1,000 in Q2 2026, at an average price of $3.61 million (+21.9%).
  • Luxury condo sales rose 11.2% to 607, at an average of $2.83 million (+4.9%).

  • The typical Miami luxury home costs 8.8 times a typical home, up from 7.6 a year earlier.

How is the Miami luxury market performing in 2026?

Strongly, especially for single-family homes. The Keyes Company and Illustrated Properties' Q2 2026 Luxury Market Report showed big gains in both transactions and prices in Miami-Dade, and the report noted that the surge did not depend on seller price reductions.

How expensive are luxury homes in Miami?

Very. Redfin's July 2026 report put Miami's median luxury home (top 5% of the metro) at about $4.86 million for the three months ending May 2026, compared with about $554,000 for a typical mid-market home. That 8.8 times gap was up from 7.6 times a year earlier, the biggest increase among major metros.

See how Miami compares nationally in the most expensive luxury housing markets in the U.S.

Are Miami luxury prices still going up?

Yes, by most measures. Average luxury single-family prices in Miami-Dade rose 21.9% year over year in Q2 2026, and Knight Frank's Prime Global Cities Index showed Miami prime prices up 3.9% over the year to Q2 2026. Different reports measure different slices of the market, so growth rates vary by source.

Single-family homes or condos: where is the demand?

Single-family homes are leading. Luxury house sales grew almost three times faster than luxury condo sales in Miami-Dade in Q2 2026 (32.5% versus 11.2%), and average house prices rose much faster too. Waterfront single-family homes, in particular, are scarce, which supports prices.

Condos remain an important part of the market, especially for second-home and international buyers. Our article on pre-construction luxury condos covers that side.

Who is buying luxury homes in Miami?

Miami draws domestic buyers relocating from higher-tax states, second-home buyers and international buyers. Florida has no state personal income tax, which is one reason the state attracts high earners and retirees. Lifestyle, climate and a growing business scene play a big role too.

For agents, this means many buyers start their search from another city or country, often on their phones. Video and social media matter even more when buyers can't easily tour in person.

posts.excerpt: Luxury is relative. Here's how the industry defines it, why the threshold changes by city and which features buyers expect at the top of the market.
posts.html:
A luxury home is usually defined as a property in the top 5% to 10% of prices in its local market. There is no single national dollar threshold: Redfin, for example, defines luxury as the top 5% of each metro by estimated value, which works out to about $1 million in Columbus, Ohio, but more than $4.8 million in Miami.

Beyond price, luxury homes share a mix of location, quality, privacy and lifestyle features.

Key takeaways

  • Luxury is relative to the local market, usually the top 5% to 10% of prices.
  • The U.S. median luxury home sold for about $1.39 million in early 2026 (Redfin).
  • Luxury thresholds range from about $1 million to almost $5 million depending on the metro.
  • Location, design, materials, privacy and views matter as much as size.
  • Many agencies, including ours, focus on furnished homes from about $1.5 million and up.

How is a luxury home defined?

Most data providers define luxury by price rank within a local market. Redfin uses the top 5% of homes in each metro by estimated market value. Other analysts use the top 10% or a fixed local price floor. Because home values vary so much between cities, a percentile is more useful than a single national number.

Nationally, Redfin put the median luxury home sale price at about $1.39 million for the three months ending April 2026. In individual metros, the typical luxury home ranged widely:

What features make a home luxury?

Location comes first, then quality and experience. Common features of luxury homes include:

  • Prime location: waterfront, views, top neighborhoods, privacy.
  • Architecture and design: a recognized architect or builder, custom layouts.
  • Materials: natural stone, custom millwork, high-end appliances.
  • Outdoor living: pools, terraces, outdoor kitchens, docks, gardens.
  • Wellness and leisure: gyms, spas, wine rooms, theaters.
  • Technology: smart home systems, security, energy features.
  • Space for living and hosting: guest suites, entertaining areas.

No single feature makes a home luxury. It is the combination, and how it all feels together.

Is luxury real estate only about price?

No. Price sets the threshold, but buyers at the top of the market pay for rarity and experience. Two homes at the same price can feel completely different. The one with a better location, view or design usually wins.

How does luxury change from city to city?

In a lower-priced metro, a $1.2 million home with modern finishes and a large lot may be luxury. In Miami or Los Angeles, luxury often means waterfront, views or a top neighborhood, at several million dollars and up. Agents should always define luxury in terms of their own market.

posts.html:
Luxury real estate investing means buying high-end property to grow wealth through appreciation, rental income or both. Common strategies include buying in markets with rising luxury prices, renting homes as luxury vacation or seasonal rentals, buying pre-construction and renovating to resell. Returns can be strong, but the luxury segment has fewer buyers, so liquidity and carrying costs need careful planning.

This guide covers the main strategies, the risks and how to choose well. It is educational, not financial advice.

Key takeaways

  • Luxury property can appreciate well, but it can take longer to sell than mid-market homes.
  • Choose markets with demand drivers: jobs, migration, lifestyle, limited supply.
  • Plan for high carrying costs: taxes, insurance, HOA fees and maintenance.
  • Location and rarity protect value better than finishes.
  • Talk to a licensed financial advisor, tax professional and attorney before investing.

What are the main ways to invest in luxury real estate?

There are five common strategies:

Strategy How it makes money Main risk
Buy and hold Long-term appreciation Market cycles, carrying costs
Luxury vacation or seasonal rental Rental income plus appreciation Rules, vacancy, management costs
Pre-construction Buying early at today's price Delays, market changes before completion
Renovate and resell Adding value through improvements Overspending, slow resale
Long-term luxury rental Steady rent from executives or relocating families Lower yield than mid-market rentals

Each one suits different goals. Our guides to luxury vacation rentals and pre-construction condos go deeper.

Is luxury real estate a good investment in 2026?

It can be, in the right market. Redfin reported that the U.S. median luxury home price rose 3.6% year over year in the three months ending April 2026, with much stronger gains in metros like Tampa (17.1%) and Las Vegas (16.1%) and small declines in New York and Denver. Market choice matters more than the national trend.

See the full data in our 2026 luxury market report.

How do you choose a market for luxury investment?

Look for long-term demand drivers and limited supply. Useful signals include:

  • Population and wealth migration into the area.
  • Job growth in high-paying industries.
  • Lifestyle appeal: climate, waterfront, culture, schools.
  • Limited land for new luxury homes, such as waterfront or historic districts.
  • Tax environment. Florida, Texas, Tennessee and Nevada, for example, have no state personal income tax, which attracts high earners.
  • Recent sales activity in the luxury segment, not just prices.

Our list of the best places to invest in luxury real estate applies these signals.

What risks do luxury investors underestimate?

The biggest are liquidity and carrying costs. There are fewer buyers at high price points, so selling can take longer, especially in a slow market. Meanwhile, taxes, insurance, HOA fees, staff and maintenance continue every month.

Other risks:

  • Insurance costs, especially in coastal and wildfire-prone areas.
  • Rental restrictions from cities or HOAs.
  • Over-improvement, where renovations cost more than buyers will pay.
  • Concentration, with one expensive asset representing a large share of your wealth.

How do you protect the resale value of a luxury property?

Buy the best location you can afford, keep the home in excellent condition and avoid highly personal design choices. When it is time to sell, present it at the level buyers expect: professional photos, cinematic video and a strong launch plan.

Cost Notes

Transaction costs Commissions, closing costs, transfer taxes

Should you work with a real estate agent as an investor?

Yes. A local luxury agent knows neighborhood values, upcoming listings and what buyers will pay at resale. Pair that with a financial advisor, tax professional and real estate attorney.

Sometimes. Redfin reported luxury prices rising faster than non-luxury prices in spring 2026, but this changes by market and over time.

It can be, but rental yields on luxury homes are often lower than on mid-market properties, and rules on short-term rentals vary. See our luxury vacation rental guide.

No real estate investment is risk-free. Prime locations with lasting demand and limited supply tend to hold value best over time.

A luxury vacation rental can be a good investment when three things line up: local rules allow short-term rentals, nightly rates and occupancy cover the high costs of running a premium home and the property is marketed well enough to stay booked. Many luxury rentals earn less on paper than expected because of cleaning, management, furnishing and seasonal gaps, so run conservative numbers first.

Here is how to evaluate one. This is educational content, not financial advice.

Key takeaways

  • Check city, county and HOA rules before anything else.
  • Model income conservatively, with realistic occupancy and seasonality.
  • Luxury rentals carry higher costs: management, cleaning, maintenance, furnishings, insurance.
  • Guests book with their eyes. Photos and video drive bookings and nightly rates.
  • Have a backup plan, like long-term or seasonal rental, if rules change.

Are luxury vacation rentals profitable?

They can be, but profit depends on location, rules, occupancy and costs. Premium homes earn high nightly rates, yet they also cost more to clean, staff, maintain and insure. The best performers sit in destinations with year-round demand and are presented beautifully.

What should you check before buying a luxury vacation rental?

Start with the rules. Many cities, counties and homeowner associations restrict or ban short-term rentals, require permits or limit the number of nights. A rule change can wipe out the business plan overnight.

Then check:

  • Demand: Is the area a year-round or seasonal destination?
  • Competition: How many similar luxury rentals are listed nearby?
  • Access: Airports, beaches, ski lifts or attractions.
  • Insurance: Availability and cost for short-term rentals.
  • Taxes: Local lodging or tourist taxes you will need to collect.

How do you run the numbers on a luxury rental?

Estimate income and subtract every cost. Use conservative assumptions and compare the result against the full cost of owning the home.

Line item What to include
Gross income Nightly rate x booked nights, by season
Platform fees Booking site fees
Management Often a percentage of income
Cleaning and laundry Per stay
Maintenance Pool, landscaping, repairs, wear and tear
Utilities and services Power, internet, streaming, supplies
Insurance Short-term rental coverage
Taxes Property taxes, lodging taxes
Furnishing and refresh Initial setup and regular updates
Financing Mortgage payments if applicable

If the numbers only work at very high occupancy, treat that as a warning sign.

How do you set nightly rates for a luxury rental?

Base rates on comparable luxury rentals nearby, adjusted for season, events and minimum stays. Higher-end guests often book further ahead and stay longer, so minimum night requirements are common. Review rates regularly against your booking pace.

  • Lead booking-site listings with your strongest photos.

It depends on the market and your goals. Short-term rentals can earn more per night but take more work and face more regulation. Long-term luxury rentals to executives or relocating families offer steadier income with less management. Our luxury real estate investing guide compares strategies.

Location, design, amenities (pool, views, chef's kitchen, spa features), high-end furnishings and excellent service. Presentation matters as much as the home.

Upgrade photos and video, refine the listing copy around the guest experience and use social media and ads to reach travelers directly.
