posts.html:
Buying a pre-construction luxury condo means signing a contract on a unit before the building is finished, usually with staged deposits and the balance due at closing. The appeal is buying at today's price, choosing the best units and finishes and potentially gaining value by completion. The risks include construction delays, market changes, financing hurdles and a finished product that differs from the renderings.

Here is how it works and what to check. This is educational content, not financial or legal advice.

Key takeaways

  • You pay deposits over time and close when the building is complete.
  • Early buyers often get better pricing and unit selection.
  • Delays and market changes are the main risks.
  • Research the developer's track record and read the contract with an attorney.
  • Renderings are not the final product. Ask for specs in writing.

How does buying a pre-construction condo work?

You reserve a unit, sign a purchase contract and pay deposits in stages, often at signing, at certain construction milestones and at closing. The deposit structure varies by project and state. When the building is complete and receives approval to be occupied, you close and pay the balance, either in cash or with a mortgage.

What are the benefits of pre-construction luxury condos?

Benefit Why it matters
Early pricing Prices often rise as a project sells and nears completion
Unit selection Early buyers get the best views, floors and layouts
Customization Finish and upgrade choices on some projects
Brand-new building Modern amenities, systems and design
Time to plan Deposits are spread out before closing

What are the risks?

The main risks are time and uncertainty. Construction can be delayed, the market can shift before you close, financing conditions can change and the finished building may differ from what you imagined.

Other risks to consider:

  • Developer risk: financial strength and track record.
  • Contract terms: what happens if the project is delayed or changed.
  • Assignment limits: some contracts restrict reselling before closing.
  • HOA fees: final fees may differ from early estimates.
  • Appraisal gaps: if values change, financing may be affected.

What should you check before buying pre-construction?

Use this checklist:

  1. Developer track record. Completed projects, quality and timeliness.
  2. Deposit protection. How deposits are held under your state's rules.
  3. Contract terms. Delays, changes, cancellation and assignment rights.
  4. Specifications. Finishes and features listed in writing, not just in renderings.
  5. Estimated HOA fees and what they cover.
  6. Rental rules. Whether short-term or long-term rentals are allowed.
  7. Financing. Pre-approval and lender requirements for new condos.
  8. Location fundamentals. Demand, views, access and future development nearby.

Always have a real estate attorney review the contract.

It depends on the market and the project. In Miami-Dade, for example, luxury condo sales rose 11.2% and the average luxury condo price rose 4.9% in Q2 2026, according to The Keyes Company and Illustrated Properties, while in Palm Beach County the average luxury condo price fell 7.1%. See our Miami luxury market report for more on South Florida condos.

Agents and developers market pre-construction with renderings, model units, sales galleries, video and lifestyle storytelling. Because buyers cannot walk through the finished home, cinematic video that shows the views, amenities and daily life is especially valuable. Keep marketing accurate and clearly label renderings as illustrations.

It varies by project and location. Deposits are typically paid in stages, and the total can be a significant share of the price. Review the schedule in your contract.

Sometimes, through an assignment, if the contract allows it. Many contracts limit or charge fees for assignments, so check before you buy.

Your contract sets out what happens. Some allow extensions, others give buyers certain rights after long delays. An attorney can explain your options.

It is a good idea. An agent can help compare projects, negotiate terms and represent your interests, often at no direct cost to the buyer in new developments.

posts.html:
Waterfront property can be one of the best luxury investments because the supply of waterfront land is fixed. But it comes with extra checks: the condition of the seawall and dock, water depth and boat access, flood zone and elevation, insurance costs, permits and how exposed the home is to storms. Skipping these can turn a dream home into an expensive problem.

Here is a 15-point checklist. This is educational content, not financial or legal advice.

Key takeaways

  • Waterfront land is limited, which supports long-term value.
  • Inspect the seawall, dock and lifts separately from the house.
  • Check flood zone, elevation and insurance costs before making an offer.
  • Water depth, bridges and access to open water matter to boaters.
  • Views and frontage are major value drivers. Protect them.

Why is waterfront property a popular luxury investment?

Waterfront homes are popular because they combine lifestyle with scarcity. You cannot create more shoreline, so well-located waterfront property tends to stay in demand. Views, boating and privacy also make these homes among the most desirable in any market.

What should you check before buying waterfront property?

Structure and water access

  1. Seawall condition. Age, cracks, repairs and estimated remaining life. Replacement can be expensive.
  2. Dock and boat lift. Condition, size and permits.
  3. Water depth. Enough depth for the boat you want, at low tide.
  4. Bridges and access. Fixed bridges limit boat height. Check the route to open water.
  5. Frontage. Linear feet of water frontage, a key value factor.

Risk and insurance

  1. Flood zone. Check the official flood map designation.
  2. Elevation. Finished floor elevation and any elevation certificate.
  3. Flood insurance. Get quotes before your offer, not after.
  4. Windstorm insurance. In coastal areas, a major ongoing cost.
  5. Storm history. Past damage, claims and repairs.

Rules and value

  1. Permits. Any unpermitted docks, seawalls or additions.
  2. Environmental rules. Restrictions on building near the water or mangroves.
  3. View protection. What could be built next door or across the water.
  4. HOA or community rules. Dock use, boat size, rentals.
  5. Resale comps. Recent waterfront sales, not just general neighborhood sales.

How much does waterfront add to property value?

It varies a lot by market, view, frontage and access. Open-water views and deep-water access usually command the highest premiums. Use recent waterfront sales in the same area as your guide, and see how to value a luxury home for why comps are tricky at the top.

What are the biggest risks of waterfront ownership?

The biggest risks are storm and flood exposure, rising insurance costs and expensive structural repairs like seawall replacement. Rules on building and rebuilding near the water can also limit what you can do. Budget for these from day one.

Risk How to reduce it
Flood damage Higher elevation, flood insurance, resilient construction
Seawall failure Inspection, maintenance reserve
Insurance cost increases Get quotes early, consider mitigation upgrades
Storm damage Impact windows, shutters, roof upgrades
Regulation changes Check permits and local plans

Which luxury waterfront markets are in demand?

South Florida remains one of the most active waterfront luxury regions in the U.S. In Q2 2026, Miami-Dade luxury single-family sales rose 32.5% and Palm Beach County's rose 24.2%, according to The Keyes Company and Illustrated Properties. Read more in our Miami market report.

Lead with the water. Show the view from inside, the dock at sunrise, the boat heading out and evenings on the terrace. Aerial shots and twilight images help, and a cinematic video ties it all together. See our luxury real estate video marketing guide.

Is waterfront property a good investment?

It can be, thanks to limited supply and strong demand, but it carries extra costs and risks like insurance and seawall maintenance. Evaluate both before buying.

A seawall is a structure that protects the land from the water. Its condition affects safety, value and future costs, so have it inspected separately.

Look up the property on official flood maps and ask for the elevation certificate. Your insurance agent can also help.

A permitted, well-maintained dock in deep water usually adds significant appeal for boating buyers.

posts.excerpt: The essentials for international buyers looking at Florida luxury homes, from how the purchase works to the tax rules that apply when you sell.
posts.html:
Yes, foreign buyers can generally purchase real estate in Florida, including luxury homes and condos. The process is similar to a domestic purchase, but international buyers should plan for financing differences, U.S. tax obligations, FIRPTA withholding when they sell and possibly specific state rules depending on their country. A local agent, real estate attorney and cross-border tax advisor are essential.

Here are the basics. This is general information, not legal or tax advice.

Key takeaways

  • Most foreign nationals can buy property in Florida.
  • Many international luxury buyers pay cash. Financing is possible but often needs larger down payments.
  • When a foreign person sells U.S. property, FIRPTA generally requires withholding, commonly 15% of the sale price.
  • Florida has no state personal income tax, but federal taxes still apply.
  • Laws change. Work with a Florida real estate attorney and an international tax advisor.

Can foreigners buy property in Florida?

In general, yes. Foreign nationals can buy homes, condos and land in Florida. However, Florida has adopted restrictions on property purchases by individuals and entities connected to certain countries, and rules can change. Ask a Florida real estate attorney to confirm what applies to you before you make an offer.

How does the buying process work?

The process typically follows these steps:

  1. Assemble your team: agent, attorney, tax advisor, lender if financing.
  2. Define the search: location, budget, property type, how you will use it.
  3. Tour, often remotely first. Video tours and cinematic listing videos help international buyers shortlist homes.
  4. Make an offer and sign a purchase contract.
  5. Due diligence: inspections, title search, condo or HOA documents.
  6. Funding: wire funds or finalize financing.
  7. Closing: sign documents (sometimes remotely) and receive the deed.

Can foreign buyers get a mortgage in Florida?

Some lenders offer loans to foreign nationals, often with larger down payments and more documentation than for U.S. residents. Many international luxury buyers purchase with cash. Talk to lenders that specialize in foreign national loans.

What taxes do foreign buyers pay?

Owners pay annual property taxes like any other owner. If you rent the property out, U.S. tax rules on rental income may apply. Florida does not have a state personal income tax, but federal taxes still apply. Your home country may also tax the income or gain.

What is FIRPTA?

FIRPTA (the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act) generally requires the buyer to withhold a portion of the sale price when a foreign person sells U.S. real estate, commonly 15% of the gross sales price, with some exceptions and reduced rates. The withholding is applied against the seller's U.S. tax liability. Plan for it before you buy, and ask a tax advisor how it applies to you.

Should you buy in your own name or through a company?

It depends on taxes, privacy, estate planning and liability. Some buyers use a U.S. or foreign entity, others buy personally. Each option has different tax effects, so get professional advice before closing.

Which Florida markets attract international luxury buyers?

South Florida, including Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties, has long attracted international buyers thanks to its climate, waterfront living and connections to Latin America and Europe. See our Miami luxury market report and Palm Beach vs. Miami comparison.

What should agents do to serve international buyers?

  • Offer remote touring with high-quality video.
  • Provide captions and clear, simple listing information.
  • Connect buyers with attorneys, lenders and tax advisors.
  • Be ready for time zones and remote closings.

International buyers compare Florida with other global cities. See where the world's wealthy are buying.

Frequently asked questions

Do foreigners pay more taxes on Florida property?

Annual property taxes are generally the same, but foreign owners may face different rules on rental income and must plan for FIRPTA withholding when they sell. A tax advisor can explain your situation.

Can I buy a Florida home without visiting?

Yes, many international buyers do, using video tours, remote inspections and remote closings. Still, seeing the area in person is recommended when possible.

Does buying property give me a U.S. visa?

Buying a home does not by itself grant immigration status. Speak with an immigration attorney about your options.

Do I need a U.S. bank account?

It can make paying taxes, insurance and utilities easier. Requirements vary by bank.

posts.excerpt: Luxury pricing is part science, part judgment. Here's how agents value one-of-a-kind homes when there are few true comparables.
posts.html:
Luxury homes are valued using comparable sales, like any home, but at the top of the market there are often few true comps. Agents adjust for location, views, lot size, frontage, architecture, condition and rarity, then test the price against active competition and buyer feedback. The result is a price range and a strategy, not a single "correct" number.

Here is how agents value high-end homes and build a pricing story sellers trust.

Key takeaways

  • There are fewer luxury sales, so comps are thinner and less alike.
  • Location, views and rarity drive value more than square footage.
  • Use a range, then refine it with active listings and early buyer feedback.
  • Overpricing a luxury launch wastes the weeks of highest attention.
  • Marketing affects price: presentation helps buyers see the value.

Why is it hard to value a luxury home?

It is hard because luxury homes are often unique and sell less frequently. In a typical neighborhood, there may be dozens of similar recent sales. At the top of the market, there may be only a few, and each might have a different view, lot, design or level of finish.

National data shows how stretched the top end is. In Redfin's July 2026 report, the typical luxury home cost 3.6 times a typical home nationally and nearly 9 times in Miami and West Palm Beach. Bigger gaps mean fewer homes that truly compare.

What factors drive the value of a luxury home?

Factor Why it matters
Location Street, neighborhood, privacy and prestige
Views Water, skyline, golf or nature views add major value
Waterfront and frontage Limited supply, especially deep water
Lot size Space and privacy are scarce in prime areas
Architecture and builder Recognized names and design quality
Condition and age Renovated or new versus dated
Amenities Pool, guest house, wine room, gym, dock
Rarity One of few homes with a certain feature

Square footage still matters, but price per square foot is a weaker guide at the top, because a great view or lot can be worth more than extra space.

How do agents choose luxury comparables?

Agents look for the closest matches in location and quality, then widen the search carefully. That can mean going back further in time, looking at nearby neighborhoods or including off-market and private sales they know about. Each comp is adjusted for differences in view, lot, size and condition.

For waterfront homes, use waterfront sales only. Our waterfront property checklist explains the features that move value.

What is the best pricing strategy for a luxury listing?

Price within a well-supported range and launch with strong marketing, then listen to the market. The first two weeks bring the most attention, so starting too high can waste them. If showings come but offers don't, the market is giving feedback.

Many sellers want to "test the market" at a high price. Explain the cost: a stale listing can end up selling for less after a long time on market. Our article on why luxury homes don't sell covers this in detail.

Help buyers see the value behind the price. A cinematic listing video shows the view, the light and the lifestyle that justify a luxury price. Create My Free Video.

Should you get an appraisal for a luxury home?

An appraisal from a licensed appraiser with luxury experience can help, especially for unique properties or when financing is involved. Lenders will usually order their own appraisal for a buyer's loan. An agent's market analysis and an appraisal serve different purposes and can differ.

How does marketing affect the price a luxury home sells for?

Marketing affects price because buyers pay for what they can see and feel. Strong photography, cinematic video and a clear lifestyle story help buyers understand why a home is worth more than the house down the street. A great home presented poorly can look overpriced.

See our luxury marketing playbook for the full launch plan.

How should agents present pricing to sellers?

Present a clear story: the comps, the adjustments, the active competition and the range you recommend. Then show the launch plan that will put the home in front of the right buyers. Sellers trust a price more when they can see the reasoning and the marketing behind it. Our luxury listing presentation guide shows how.

Frequently asked questions

How do you price a one-of-a-kind luxury home?

Use the closest comparable sales, adjust for differences, look at active competition and set a range. Then watch early buyer feedback and be ready to adjust.

Are online home value estimates accurate for luxury homes?

They are often less reliable at the top of the market, because there are fewer similar sales for the algorithms to use. A local luxury agent or appraiser will usually give a better estimate.

What adds the most value to a luxury home?

Location and views add the most, followed by lot size, waterfront access and quality of design. Many of these cannot be changed, which is why they hold value.

Does a price reduction hurt a luxury home's value?

A well-timed reduction paired with fresh marketing can bring new buyers. Repeated small cuts without new marketing tend to signal that something is wrong.

TikTok works for luxury realtors when the content feels premium and useful: cinematic listing tours, neighborhood guides, honest market takes and behind-the-scenes looks at high-end sales. You don't need trends or dances. You need a strong first two seconds, captions and a consistent point of view.

Here is how to make TikTok fit a luxury brand.

Key takeaways

  • TikTok shows your videos to people who don't follow you yet, which makes it a discovery channel.
  • Luxury content does well when it's cinematic, calm and specific.
  • Hook viewers in the first two seconds with a view, a price or a question.
  • Post consistently. Three to five videos a week is a realistic target.
  • The same vertical videos can run on Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.

Is TikTok worth it for luxury real estate agents?

Yes, if you treat it as a discovery and brand channel rather than a place to sell a specific home overnight. Luxury home tours are some of the most watched real estate content on the platform, and the people watching include future buyers, sellers and other agents who refer business.

Many sellers will look up your social profiles before they invite you to pitch. A polished TikTok shows them how you present homes.

What kind of TikTok content works for luxury homes?

Content that works shows something viewers can't easily see elsewhere: a home's best moments, a neighborhood's character or a straight answer about the market.

Content type Example
Cinematic listing tour A 30-second story of a day in the home
Price-point comparison "What $4M buys in three neighborhoods"
Single-detail reveal The hidden wine room, the rooftop, the dock
Market take "Luxury prices in our city just did this"
Behind the scenes Preparing a listing for launch
Neighborhood guide A perfect Saturday in the area

For more ideas, see our list of Instagram Reels ideas for luxury realtors. Most of them work on TikTok too.

How do you keep TikTok content feeling premium?

Keep it calm and well made. Use smooth camera movement, natural light, clean captions and music that fits the home. Skip loud sound effects, busy stickers and trends that clash with the listing.

A cinematic listing video does a lot of this for you. It gives you a polished hero video, and you can cut shorter clips from it for the rest of the week.

What makes a strong TikTok hook for real estate?

A strong hook gives viewers a reason to stay in the first two seconds. Lead with the most striking visual or a line that creates curiosity.

  • "This is the view you get for $6 million in [city]."
  • "Nobody expects what's behind this door."
  • "Here's what luxury buyers are asking for right now."
  • "I timed the drive from this house to the beach."

Our guide to real estate video hooks has more.

How often should luxury realtors post on TikTok?

Three to five times a week is a good target for most agents. Consistency matters more than volume. Batch your filming and editing, and lean on listing videos you already have.

Should you post the same videos on TikTok and Instagram?

Yes. Vertical videos work on TikTok, Instagram Reels, Facebook Reels and YouTube Shorts. Upload the original file to each platform rather than a version with another app's watermark.

How do you turn TikTok views into clients?

Make the next step obvious. Put a clear line in your profile ("Selling a luxury home in [area]? Message me"), link to your website and reply to comments and messages quickly. Mention your listing presentation in videos about how you market homes. See our guide to the luxury listing presentation.

Frequently asked questions

Do luxury buyers use TikTok?

Many people who could buy or sell luxury homes use TikTok, and many more watch luxury home content for inspiration. It's also a strong channel for reaching other agents who refer clients.

How long should a real estate TikTok be?

Most listing and market videos work best at 15 to 45 seconds. Longer videos can work if the opening hooks the viewer.

Do I need to dance or follow trends?

No. Luxury agents usually do better with calm, cinematic and informative videos than with trends that don't fit the brand.

Can I run ads on TikTok for listings?

TikTok offers ads, and housing ads must follow its policies and fair housing rules. Many agents start with organic content and use Meta ads for listing campaigns. See our Facebook ads guide for luxury listings.

posts.excerpt: Twelve ideas for luxury open houses and broker opens that feel like an occasion, plus how to turn attendance into offers.
posts.html:
The best luxury open house ideas turn a showing into an experience: a private, invitation-led event with thoughtful hospitality, a clear story about the home and a smooth follow-up. Think broker previews with a chef, twilight viewings, a cinematic video playing in the main room and a printed brochure with a QR code guests can share.

Here are 12 ideas, and how to make them pay off.

Key takeaways

  • Luxury open houses work best as curated events, not drop-in afternoons.
  • Start with a broker open. Agents bring the buyers.
  • Show the home at its best time of day, often twilight.
  • Give every guest something to take away and share.
  • Follow up within 24 hours with the video and next steps.

Do open houses work for luxury homes?

They can, especially when they are curated. Many luxury sellers prefer private showings for security and privacy, but a well-planned broker open or invitation-only event builds buzz, reaches agents with qualified buyers and creates content you can share.

12 luxury open house ideas

  1. Broker preview breakfast. Invite top local agents for coffee and pastries before the public launch.
  2. Twilight viewing. Show the home when the lighting, pool and views look their best.
  3. Chef or sommelier pairing. Highlight the kitchen or wine room with a short tasting.
  4. Cinematic video on loop. Play the listing video on the main screen so guests feel the full story.
  5. Neighborhood partners. Invite a local florist, design studio or restaurant to co-host.
  6. Live music. A soft acoustic set suits large living spaces and terraces.
  7. Themed tour. Walk guests through "a day in the home," from the morning coffee spot to the evening terrace.
  8. Designer or architect talk. Ten minutes on the home's design adds meaning.
  9. Private appointment slots. Combine the event with scheduled private tours for serious buyers.
  10. Printed brochure with QR code. Link to the video and property page.
  11. Photo moment. A beautiful spot for guests to take photos and share.
  12. Concierge check-in. Greet every guest, collect contact details and note interest.

Give your open house a centerpiece. A cinematic listing video playing in the great room sets the mood and gives guests something to share. Wonder Ads delivers in 48 hours. Create My Free Video.

How do you invite the right people to a luxury open house?

Invite agents first, then qualified buyers, then your wider network. Send a short teaser video to local and relocation agents, share a private invitation with your sphere and promote the event on social media without publishing the full address if your seller prefers privacy.

How do you keep a luxury open house secure?

Use registration, check-in and enough staff to accompany guests. Ask sellers to remove valuables, prescriptions and personal documents. For high-profile homes, limit attendance to registered guests and agents with qualified buyers.

What should guests take home?

Give every guest a printed brochure with the key details, floor plan and a QR code linking to the cinematic video and property page. The video lets buyers rewatch the home with their partner or family, which keeps the listing top of mind after the event.

How do you follow up after a luxury open house?

Follow up within 24 hours. Thank every guest, send the video link and floor plan and invite serious buyers to a private showing. Ask attending agents for feedback on price and presentation.

Follow-up When
Thank-you email with video and brochure Same day or next morning
Feedback request to attending agents Within 48 hours
Private showing invitations Within 48 hours
Event recap reel on social media Within a week

For the full launch plan, see our luxury listing marketing playbook.

What is a broker open?

A broker open is an event for real estate agents to preview a new listing. It helps agents with qualified buyers see the home early and gives you feedback before the public launch.

How long should a luxury open house last?

Two to three hours is typical for an event. Private appointment slots can run before or after.

Should I serve food and drinks?

Light, high-quality hospitality fits a luxury event. Keep it simple and check local rules and your brokerage's policy on serving alcohol.

Do open houses help win listings?

Yes. A memorable event shows neighbors and future sellers how you market homes. Share a recap reel afterwards to extend the reach.

posts.excerpt: One home, one page, one link for every ad and post. Here's how to build a property website that turns visitors into showings.
posts.html:
A single property website is a dedicated page or site for one listing, often on its own address like 123OceanDrive.com. For luxury homes, it should open with a cinematic video, then tell the home's story with a photo gallery, key details, floor plans, neighborhood highlights and a simple form to request a private showing.

Here is what to include and how to use it.

Key takeaways

  • A property website gives every ad, post and brochure one clean destination.
  • Lead with the cinematic video, then the story, then the details.
  • Keep the inquiry form short: name, email, phone, preferred time.
  • Track visits and inquiries so you can report results to sellers.
  • It also impresses sellers when you present your marketing plan.

Why do luxury listings need a single property website?

Portal pages are crowded with ads, other listings and distractions. A dedicated page focuses entirely on one home and gives buyers the full experience. It also gives you control: your branding, your story and your inquiry form.

It's the perfect destination for paid ads. See our Facebook ads guide for luxury listings.

What should a luxury property website include?

Section What it does
Hero video Sets the mood in seconds
Headline and short story Names what makes the home rare
Photo gallery Full set in high resolution
Key details Price, beds, baths, size, lot, features
Floor plans Helps serious buyers picture the layout
Neighborhood Lifestyle, schools, dining, commute
Agent details Your photo, name and contact
Inquiry form Request a private showing

Keep the page fast and easy to use on a phone, where most visitors will see it.

Start the page with a premiere. A cinematic video at the top of your property website shows buyers the lifestyle before they scroll. Create My Free Video.

How do you write the story section?

Write two or three short paragraphs about life in the home, then list the facts. Lead with moments and feelings, follow with features. Our guide to writing luxury listing descriptions has examples.

Should a property website have its own domain?

A custom address like the street name is memorable and looks premium on signs and brochures. A page on your own website works too and builds your site over time. Many agents use a custom domain that points to a page on their main site.

How do you drive traffic to a property website?

Link it everywhere: social posts, paid ads, email announcements, the brochure QR code and your listing presentation follow-up. Use the cinematic video in ads and send viewers to the page to learn more.

What should you track?

Track visits, video plays, time on page and inquiries. Share a simple weekly report with sellers. It shows the marketing is working and builds trust during the listing period.

Do single property websites help SEO?

They can rank for the address and building name, which helps when buyers search for a specific home. The bigger value is giving every campaign a focused destination that converts visitors into showing requests.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a single property website cost?

It depends on the tool. Many templates and listing platforms offer property pages at low cost, and custom designs cost more. The video and photos usually matter more than the design.

Should the price be on the property website?

Usually yes. Buyers expect it, and it saves time for everyone. Some ultra-luxury listings use "price upon request," but that can reduce inquiries.

What happens to the site after the home sells?

Mark it as sold and keep it as part of your portfolio, or redirect it to your website. Sold pages show future sellers how you present homes.

Can I reuse the page design for every listing?

Yes. A consistent design helps build your brand. See how to build a luxury realtor personal brand.

posts.excerpt: Your email list is the one audience you own. Here's how luxury agents use it for listing launches, market updates and repeat business.
posts.html:
Email marketing works for luxury realtors because it reaches people who already know you: past clients, your sphere, other agents and serious buyers. The best emails are short, visual and useful. Send a listing announcement with a cinematic video, a monthly market note and a personal check-in a few times a year.

Here is what to send, plus templates you can adapt.

Key takeaways

  • Email reaches people you already know, which makes it one of your highest-trust channels.
  • Segment your list: past clients, sphere, agents and active buyers.
  • Lead listing emails with a video thumbnail and one clear button.
  • Keep subject lines short and specific.
  • Follow email and privacy laws: get consent and include an unsubscribe link.

Who should luxury realtors email?

Segment your list into groups so each email feels relevant:

Segment What they want
Past clients Market updates, home value insight, personal check-ins
Sphere and friends Occasional updates and stories
Agents and brokers New listings and coming-soon previews
Active buyers Homes that match their search
Potential sellers Market insight and how you market homes

What emails should luxury agents send?

Send a few types on a steady rhythm:

  1. Listing launch. The day a new listing goes live.
  2. Coming soon. A teaser to agents and buyers before launch.
  3. Monthly market note. One insight, one chart or number, one takeaway.
  4. Just sold. A short story of how the home sold.
  5. Personal check-in. A few times a year, no pitch.

What does a great listing launch email look like?

Short, visual and focused on one action. Use a video thumbnail that links to the property page, three lines about the lifestyle, the key details and a button to book a private showing.

Subject: Just listed: the bayfront home with the private dock

Mornings on the water. Lunch by the pool. The skyline at night.

[Video thumbnail: Watch the video] → links to your property page

6 beds · 7 baths · 70 ft of frontage · $8,950,000

[Book a private showing]

Emails with video get noticed. Add a cinematic listing video thumbnail to your next launch email. Wonder Ads delivers ready-to-share videos in 48 hours. Create My Free Video.

What subject lines work for luxury real estate emails?

Short, specific and curious subject lines work best. Avoid all caps and hype words.

  • "Just listed: the home with the rooftop pool"
  • "What $5M buys in [neighborhood] right now"
  • "Luxury prices in [city]: one number to know"
  • "A private preview, before it hits the market"
  • "Sold in 21 days. Here's what we did."

Only use real results from your own sales.

What should a monthly market email include?

One clear insight, one supporting number and what it means for the reader. Link to a longer post for those who want more. Our 2026 luxury market report is an example of the kind of data that works.

How often should you email your list?

Monthly is a good baseline for market notes, plus listing announcements as they happen. Watch unsubscribes and replies. If people engage, keep going. If they don't, send less and make each email more useful.

What rules apply to real estate email marketing?

Get permission before adding people to marketing emails, include your business address and make unsubscribing easy. Rules vary by country and state, so check the laws that apply to you and your brokerage policy.

Frequently asked questions

Is email marketing still effective for realtors?

Yes. Email reaches people who already know and trust you, and it's one of the few channels you own. It works best when emails are short and useful.

Which email platform should I use?

Most agents use a CRM or email tool that supports segments and templates. Pick one you'll actually use every month.

Should I send listings to my whole list?

Send new listings to agents and active buyers, and share only special listings with your wider sphere. Relevance keeps people subscribed.

How do I grow my email list?

Offer something useful, like a monthly luxury market note, on your website and social profiles, and add every new contact with permission.

posts.excerpt: A simple structure for luxury listing descriptions, three before-and-after examples and the clichés to cut.
posts.html:
A strong luxury listing description opens with what makes the home rare, describes two or three moments of life there, then lists the key facts clearly. Keep it specific and calm. Swap clichés like "stunning" and "entertainer's dream" for concrete details buyers can picture.

Here is the structure, plus examples you can adapt.

Key takeaways

  • Lead with the one thing that makes the home rare.
  • Describe moments, not adjectives.
  • Follow the story with clear, scannable facts.
  • Cut clichés and vague superlatives.
  • Check your MLS rules and fair housing guidelines before publishing.

What makes a luxury listing description effective?

It's effective when a buyer can picture living there after reading it. Specific details do that better than adjectives. "Watch the sunrise over the bay from your bed" says more than "breathtaking views."

What structure should a luxury listing description follow?

  1. The hook. One sentence on what makes the home rare.
  2. The story. Two or three sentences about life in the home.
  3. The details. Key features and specs, easy to scan.
  4. The location. What's nearby and why it matters.
  5. The next step. How to see it.

Example 1: Waterfront home

Before: "Stunning waterfront home with breathtaking views. Entertainer's dream with pool and dock. Must see!"

After: "Set on 70 feet of open bay, this home starts every day with the water. Coffee on the terrace, the boat ready at the private dock, long lunches by the pool and evenings watching the skyline light up across the bay. Six bedrooms, seven baths, a chef's kitchen and a primary suite that opens to the view."

Example 2: Penthouse

Before: "Luxurious penthouse with amazing city views and top-of-the-line finishes."

After: "Above the city, everything slows down. Floor-to-ceiling glass wraps the living room in light, a 1,200-square-foot terrace hosts dinner under the skyline and a private elevator opens directly into the residence."

Example 3: Family estate

Before: "Gorgeous estate perfect for families. Lots of space for entertaining."

After: "Built for family life at every scale. Weekend breakfasts around the island, kids racing to the pool, a guest house for visiting grandparents and a lawn big enough for the whole neighborhood. Minutes from top schools and the club."

Which words should you avoid in luxury listings?

Avoid Use instead
Stunning, breathtaking, amazing The specific view or feature
Entertainer's dream "Seats 12 on the terrace, steps from the outdoor kitchen"
Must see! A clear next step
Luxurious finishes Name the materials
Perfect for families Describe the spaces, not the buyer

That last one matters. Describe the property, not who should live there, to stay in line with fair housing guidelines.

How long should a luxury listing description be?

Long enough to tell the story and cover the key facts, within your MLS character limit. On your property website and brochure, you can go longer. See our guide to single property websites.

How does the description fit with the rest of your marketing?

The description, video script, captions and ads should all tell the same story. Write the positioning first, then reuse it. Our video script templates follow the same structure.

Frequently asked questions

Should a luxury listing description mention the price?

The price usually appears in its own field on the MLS and portals. In the description, focus on story and features.

Can I use AI to write listing descriptions?

AI can help with a first draft. Always check every fact against the home, remove clichés and make sure it follows MLS and fair housing rules.

How many features should I list?

Lead with the three or four that make the home rare, then list the rest briefly. Too many features in a row become a blur.

Who should write the description?

The agent who knows the home best, ideally after asking the sellers what they love most about living there.

YouTube works for luxury realtors because people search it. Buyers relocating to your city search for neighborhood guides, cost-of-living videos and luxury home tours, and those videos can bring views for years. A simple strategy: one longer video a week or every two weeks, plus Shorts cut from your listing videos.

Here is how to set it up.

Key takeaways

  • YouTube is a search engine. Title videos the way people search.
  • Neighborhood guides and home tours attract relocating buyers.
  • Shorts help new viewers find you. Long videos build trust.
  • Consistency matters more than production budget.
  • Put a clear next step in every description.

Is YouTube worth it for luxury real estate agents?

Yes, especially for agents in markets that attract relocating and second-home buyers. Unlike most social posts, a good YouTube video can keep getting found through search long after you publish it. It also shows sellers how you present homes.

What videos should luxury realtors make?

Video type Example title
Neighborhood guide "Living in [Neighborhood]: Pros and Cons"
Luxury home tour "Inside a $7M Waterfront Home in [City]"
Price comparison "What $3M Buys in [City] vs [City]"
Market update "[City] Luxury Market Update: What Changed This Quarter"
Buyer education "Buying a Luxury Home in [State]: Step by Step"
Shorts 30-second cinematic listing clips

How do you title YouTube videos so they get found?

Use the words people actually search, place names first, and a clear promise. Check YouTube's search suggestions by typing the start of a phrase. "Moving to Miami" and "Miami luxury homes" are examples of how buyers search.

Keep titles under about 60 characters so they don't get cut off, and make the thumbnail match the title.

How do YouTube Shorts help realtors?

Shorts are vertical videos under a minute that YouTube shows to people who don't follow you yet. They are a great way to reuse listing reels from Instagram and TikTok and send new viewers to your longer videos.

How long should a real estate YouTube video be?

Long enough to answer the question in the title. Home tours often run 8 to 15 minutes, neighborhood guides 10 to 20 minutes and market updates 5 to 10. Cut anything that doesn't help the viewer.

How do you turn YouTube viewers into clients?

Add a clear next step in every description and at the end of each video: book a call, get a market report or request a private showing. Pin a comment with your contact link and reply to questions quickly. Relocating buyers often reach out after watching several videos.

What gear do you need to start?

A recent phone, a small microphone and good natural light are enough to start. Listing videos you already have can fill your channel while you build the habit. Quality of information matters more than expensive gear.

Frequently asked questions

How often should I post on YouTube?

One longer video every week or two, plus a few Shorts a week, is a realistic rhythm for most agents.

Do I need to be on camera?

For neighborhood guides and market updates, appearing on camera builds trust. Home tours and Shorts can work with voiceover only.

How long does it take to get results on YouTube?

Usually months. Videos build up over time as they get found through search. Consistency is what makes the channel work.

Can I use the same videos on other platforms?

Yes. Shorts work on Reels and TikTok, and longer videos can be embedded on your website and property pages. See our TikTok guide for luxury realtors.

posts.excerpt: Room-by-room staging priorities for high-end homes, and why great staging makes your photos and cinematic video work harder.
posts.html:
Luxury home staging is about editing, not decorating. Remove personal items and clutter, highlight the home's best features, style key rooms with a few high-quality pieces and prepare outdoor spaces as carefully as indoor ones. Done well, staging helps buyers picture their own life in the home and makes every photo and video look better.

Here is where to focus.

Key takeaways

  • Edit first: declutter and depersonalize.
  • Prioritize the rooms buyers see first and photograph most.
  • Outdoor living spaces need staging too.
  • Light and scent shape how a home feels in person.
  • Stage with photos and video in mind.

Why does staging matter for luxury homes?

Buyers at high price points expect a home to feel finished. Staging helps them see the space, the light and the lifestyle instead of the current owner's belongings. It also sets up the photos and video that do most of the marketing.

Which rooms should you stage first?

Focus on the spaces buyers see first and that appear most in marketing:

Priority Room Focus
1 Living or great room Clear sightlines, a few statement pieces
2 Kitchen Clear counters, one or two styled moments
3 Primary suite Calm bedding, view toward windows
4 Outdoor living Furniture set, cushions out, pool clean
5 Dining Table styled, not overdressed

Use fewer, better pieces. Fresh flowers or greenery, quality linens, a few books or objects and art that suits the space. Leave surfaces mostly clear so the architecture and materials can shine.

How should you prepare outdoor spaces?

Treat terraces, pools and gardens as rooms. Set the furniture, put cushions out, trim landscaping, clean the pool and turn on landscape lighting for twilight photos. For waterfront homes, make the dock look ready for a day on the water.

How do light and scent affect showings?

Open blinds, turn on every light and set a comfortable temperature before showings. Keep scent subtle and clean. Buyers notice how a home feels as much as how it looks.

A real estate video hook is the first line or image that makes someone stop scrolling. For luxury listings, the strongest hooks combine a striking visual, like the view or the most unusual room, with a short line that creates curiosity, such as "Nobody expects what's behind this door." You have about two seconds to earn the next ten.

Here are 25 hooks you can use, grouped by video type.

Key takeaways

  • Open with your best visual, not the front door.
  • Pair it with a short line on screen or in voiceover.
  • Curiosity, contrast and specific numbers make strong hooks.
  • Keep the promise. The video must deliver what the hook suggests.
  • Test different hooks on the same video to see what works.

What makes a good real estate video hook?

A good hook is specific, visual and fast. It shows something interesting right away and gives viewers a reason to keep watching. Vague openers like "Welcome to this beautiful home" lose people.

Listing video hooks

  1. "This is what $6 million looks like on the water."
  2. "Nobody expects what's behind this door."
  3. "Wait until you see the view from the bed."
  4. "This kitchen has a secret."
  5. "The best room in this house isn't inside."
  6. "This home sold the owners in one minute. Here's that minute."
  7. "Morning coffee hits different here."
  8. "There are only a few homes like this in [city]."

Neighborhood video hooks

  1. "If you're moving to [city], start here."
  2. "Three places in [neighborhood] locals don't share."
  3. "I timed the drive from here to the beach."

Market update hooks

  3. "Buyers are asking for this more than anything right now."
  4. "Is now a good time to sell a luxury home? Here's the data."

Agent brand and seller hooks

How do you test hooks?

Post the same video with two different first lines, or try different first shots across similar listings, and compare how much of the video people watch. Keep what works and drop what doesn't.

One short sentence, or a few words on screen, in the first two seconds.

Should the hook be spoken or written on screen?

Both work best together. Many viewers watch with sound off, so put key words on screen as captions.

Yes. Rotate your best hooks across listings and adjust the details to fit each home.

posts.html:
To get luxury listings, pick a specific niche, become visible there, build relationships with the people luxury sellers trust and show marketing that looks as good as the homes you want to list. Many agents win their first luxury listing through a referral or a co-listing partnership, then use that sale to win the next.

Here is a practical plan.

Key takeaways

  • Focus on one neighborhood, property type or buyer type.
  • Luxury sellers hire agents they already trust or have seen at work.
  • Your marketing is your proof. Make it look high-end.
  • Partner with an established luxury agent to build experience.
  • Every listing you market well becomes a pitch for the next one.

Why is it hard to break into luxury real estate?

There are fewer luxury listings, sellers are selective and many already have relationships with established agents. They want proof that you can present and sell a high-end home. The good news: proof can be built, and marketing quality is something you control.

Step 1: Choose your luxury niche

Choose a niche where you can become the obvious expert: a waterfront neighborhood, a set of luxury buildings, new construction or buyers relocating from a specific region. See what is considered a luxury home to define the price range in your market.

Step 2: Become visible in that niche

Post neighborhood guides, market notes and listing content about your niche every week. Attend local events, broker opens and charity functions. Over time, people start to connect your name with that area.

Step 3: Build relationships with luxury influencers

Luxury sellers often ask advisors for recommendations. Build genuine relationships with wealth managers, estate attorneys, builders, architects, interior designers and concierge services. Offer value first, such as market insight for their clients.

Show sellers what you'd do with their home. A cinematic preview video built from existing photos is a powerful way to win your first luxury appointment. Your first video is free. Create My Free Video.

Step 4: Make your marketing look luxury now

Upgrade the marketing on every listing you have, whatever the price: professional photos, cinematic video and a clean, consistent brand. Sellers judge you by your current work. See our luxury marketing playbook.

Step 5: Partner on your first luxury listings

Co-list with an established luxury agent, or work on their team for a period. You gain experience, connections and a sale to point to. Offer your marketing skills as part of the partnership.

Step 6: Prepare a listing presentation that proves it

Bring your positioning, pricing logic, a 14-day launch plan and examples of your marketing. A preview video of the seller's own home stands out. Our luxury listing presentation guide walks through it.

Step 7: Turn every sale into the next listing

After each sale, share the story: a launch recap, a just-sold email and a short reel. Ask for introductions. Luxury business grows through referrals and visible results.

Months 3 to 6 Relationships, partnerships, first co-listings
Months 6 to 12 Own listings, launch recaps, referrals

Frequently asked questions

How long does it take to get your first luxury listing?

It varies widely. Agents who focus on one niche, partner with experienced agents and market consistently often get there faster.

Do I need luxury designations or certifications?

They can add credibility, but sellers care most about results and marketing quality. Use designations as a support, not a substitute.

Competing on price alone is risky. Show the value of your marketing plan instead. A strong plan changes the conversation.

posts.title: Virtual Staging vs. Real Staging for Luxury Homes: Which Is Better?
posts.seo_title: Virtual Staging vs Real Staging for Luxury Homes
posts.meta: Virtual staging vs. real staging for luxury listings: cost, speed, buyer experience, disclosure rules and when to use each, or both.
posts.excerpt: A side-by-side comparison of virtual and physical staging for high-end homes, plus the disclosure rules you can't skip.
posts.html:
Real staging is usually better for luxury homes that buyers will tour in person, because the home looks the same at the showing as it does online. Virtual staging is faster and cheaper, and works well for vacant rooms, pre-construction or a quick refresh, as long as images are clearly labeled. Many agents combine the two: physically stage the main rooms and virtually stage secondary spaces.

Here is how they compare.

Key takeaways

  • Real staging creates a consistent experience online and in person.
  • Virtual staging is faster and costs less, but buyers may feel a gap at the showing.
  • Virtually staged images must be clearly disclosed under most MLS rules.
  • A hybrid approach often works best for large luxury homes.
  • Either way, staging sets up your photos and video.

What is the difference between virtual and real staging?

Real staging places actual furniture and decor in the home. Virtual staging adds furniture and decor digitally to photos of empty or dated rooms. Both aim to help buyers picture the space, but only real staging changes what buyers see in person.

How do virtual and real staging compare?

Real staging Virtual staging
Cost Higher, often monthly rental Lower, per image
Speed Days to schedule and install Often within days
In-person experience Matches the photos Rooms are empty at the showing
Flexibility Fixed style Different styles per image
Best for Occupied or vacant luxury homes buyers will tour Vacant rooms, pre-construction, quick refreshes
Disclosure Not required Usually required by MLS rules

When is real staging the better choice?

Choose real staging for the main living spaces of a luxury home that buyers will visit, especially at higher price points. When buyers walk into the same beautiful rooms they saw online, the home feels true to its marketing. Our luxury home staging tips cover where to focus.

When does virtual staging make sense?

Virtual staging makes sense for vacant secondary rooms, homes where installing furniture is impractical, pre-construction units and quick updates to older photos. It's also helpful for showing different uses of a flexible room, like an office or gym.

Disclosure labels stay in. When Wonder Ads builds a cinematic video from virtually staged photos, the disclosure labels stay visible, and every scene is checked against the original. See how it works.

What are the rules for virtual staging?

Most MLSs require virtually staged images to be clearly labeled, and many also ask agents to include an unstaged version or a note in the remarks. Rules vary, so check your MLS and brokerage policy. Never use virtual staging to hide defects or change permanent features like floors, walls or views.

We cover this in more detail in AI listing videos and MLS rules.

Can you use virtually staged photos in a listing video?

Yes, if the disclosure stays clear. Any video made from virtually staged photos should keep the labels visible and avoid implying the furniture comes with the home.

Frequently asked questions

Is virtual staging worth it for luxury homes?

It can be for vacant secondary rooms or pre-construction. For the main spaces of a home buyers will tour, real staging usually creates a better experience.

Do buyers mind virtual staging?

Most buyers are used to it when it's clearly labeled. Problems arise when images are misleading or the gap between photos and reality feels too big.

Can I virtually remove furniture?

Virtual decluttering is common but is still an alteration. Follow your MLS rules on disclosure and never remove permanent features.

What's the best approach for a large vacant estate?

Many agents physically stage the main living areas and primary suite, then virtually stage secondary rooms with clear labels.

Buying a luxury home follows the same basic steps as any purchase, with a few differences: you'll usually need proof of funds or a jumbo loan pre-approval, many homes are marketed privately, inspections are more detailed and insurance can take longer to arrange. Working with an experienced luxury agent and a strong advisory team makes the process smoother.

Here is the process step by step.

Key takeaways

  • Have proof of funds or a jumbo pre-approval ready before you tour.
  • Some luxury homes are sold privately or before they reach the market.
  • Inspect everything: systems, roof, pool, seawall, smart-home tech.
  • Get insurance quotes early, especially in coastal areas.
  • Build a team: agent, attorney, lender or private banker, tax advisor.

Step 1: Build your team

Choose a luxury agent who knows the neighborhoods you're considering and has access to private and coming-soon listings. Add a real estate attorney, a lender or private banker and a tax advisor. NAR's 2025 buyer survey found 88% of buyers purchased through an agent or broker.

Step 2: Get your financing in order

Sellers of high-end homes usually want proof that you can close. That means a bank statement showing funds for a cash purchase or a pre-approval for a jumbo loan. Learn more in jumbo loans explained.

Step 3: Define what you want

List your must-haves (location, size, views, schools, privacy) and nice-to-haves. Be clear about how you'll use the home: primary residence, second home or investment. That decision affects financing and taxes.

Step 4: Search, including off-market

Luxury homes are often shared privately with agents and their networks before or instead of public listing. Your agent's relationships matter. Cinematic videos and property pages make it easier to shortlist homes remotely.

Agents: help remote buyers fall in love before the tour. Wonder Ads turns listing photos into cinematic videos buyers can share with family. Create My Free Video.

Step 5: Tour and evaluate

Visit at different times of day, check noise, light and privacy and explore the neighborhood. For waterfront homes, see our waterfront property checklist.

Step 6: Make an offer and negotiate

Your agent will review comparable sales and advise on price and terms. At the top of the market, comps can be thin, so terms like timing, contingencies and what furniture is included can matter as much as price. See how to value a luxury home.

Step 7: Due diligence

Check Why

Specialized inspections Pool, seawall, dock, elevator, smart-home systems
Title search Clear ownership, liens, easements
Survey Boundaries and setbacks
HOA or condo documents Rules, fees, reserves, assessments

Step 8: Close

Sign the documents, wire funds and receive the keys. Many luxury closings can be handled partly remotely. Plan movers, staff and home systems handover in advance.

If you finance a home above the conforming loan limit, yes. For 2026, the baseline limit for one-unit homes is $832,750, and up to $1,249,125 in high-cost areas.

How long does it take to buy a luxury home?

Searches can take weeks to months. Once under contract, closing often takes 30 to 60 days, depending on financing and due diligence.

What are off-market luxury listings?

Homes marketed privately to select agents and buyers rather than publicly. Sellers choose this for privacy or to test the market.

Should I buy in my own name or an LLC?

It depends on privacy, taxes and liability. See buying a luxury home through an LLC and talk to an attorney.

posts.excerpt: Plain-English definitions of the terms that come up in high-end real estate, from jumbo loans to seawalls.
posts.html:
This luxury real estate glossary defines the terms that come up most often when buying, selling or marketing high-end homes, in plain English. Bookmark it, or share it with clients who are new to the luxury market.

Key takeaways

  • Luxury deals use a few terms you won't hear in typical sales.
  • Many relate to financing (jumbo loans), privacy (off-market) or property features (frontage, seawall).
  • Investors should know 1031 exchanges and FIRPTA.
  • Marketing terms matter too: positioning, lifestyle marketing, cinematic video.

Market and pricing terms

Luxury home: A home in the top tier of its local market, often defined as the top 5% to 10% of prices. See what is considered a luxury home.

Ultra-luxury: The very top of the market, often the top 1% or homes above a high local threshold.

Prime property: The most desirable homes in a city's best locations, a term used in global market reports.

Luxury premium: How many times more a typical luxury home costs than a typical home in the same area.

Comparable sales (comps): Recent sales of similar homes used to estimate value.

Price per square foot: Price divided by living area. Less reliable at the top of the market.

Days on market (DOM): How long a listing has been active.

Absorption rate: How quickly available homes are selling in a market.

Listing and marketing terms

Off-market listing: A home sold privately without public listing.

Pocket listing: A listing an agent markets privately to select buyers or agents. MLS rules on this vary.

Coming soon: A status for homes about to be listed, where allowed by the MLS.

Broker open: An event for agents to preview a new listing. See luxury open house ideas.

Positioning: The one-sentence story of who a home is for and why it's rare.

Lifestyle marketing: Marketing that shows the life a home offers. See lifestyle marketing.

Cinematic listing video: A short, story-driven video with music, voiceover and captions.

Single property website: A dedicated page for one listing.

Virtual staging: Digitally adding furniture to photos, which usually requires disclosure.

Twilight photography: Exterior photos taken at dusk.

Cinematic listing video, defined by us. Wonder Ads creates them from your MLS photos: original music, voiceover, captions, delivered in 48 hours. Create My Free Video.

Financing and legal terms

Jumbo loan: A mortgage above the conforming loan limit. See jumbo loans explained.

Conforming loan limit: The maximum loan size eligible for purchase by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. For 2026, $832,750 for most one-unit homes.

Proof of funds: Documents showing a buyer can pay cash.

Escrow: A neutral third party holding funds or documents until closing.

Title insurance: Protection against problems with ownership records.

Appraisal: A licensed appraiser's estimate of a home's value, usually required by lenders.

Closing costs: Fees and expenses paid at closing, such as title, escrow, recording and lender fees.

Contingency: A condition in a contract, such as inspection or financing.

Assignment: Transferring a purchase contract to another buyer, common in pre-construction.

LLC purchase: Buying property through a limited liability company. See buying through an LLC.

Investment and tax terms

1031 exchange: A U.S. tax rule that lets investors defer capital gains tax by reinvesting in like-kind property. See 1031 exchanges for luxury real estate.

FIRPTA: A U.S. law that generally requires withholding when a foreign person sells U.S. real estate.

Capital gains: Profit from selling a property.

Carrying costs: Ongoing costs of owning a property: taxes, insurance, fees, maintenance.

Cap rate: Net operating income divided by property value, a rental return measure.

Appreciation: Increase in property value over time.

Property feature terms

Frontage: The length of a property along water, a road or a view.

Seawall: A structure protecting waterfront land from the water.

Deep-water access: Water deep enough for larger boats.

Guard-gated community: A neighborhood with staffed security entry.

Lock-and-leave: A home easy to leave for long periods, often a condo.

Smart home: Connected systems for lighting, climate, security and entertainment.

Frequently asked questions

What is the difference between off-market and pocket listings?

The terms overlap. Both describe homes marketed privately. MLS rules on private marketing vary, so check yours.

What does "luxury premium" mean?

It compares the price of a typical luxury home to a typical home in the same market. Redfin reported a national premium of 3.6 times in 2026.

What is a conforming loan limit?

The largest loan Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will buy. Loans above it are jumbo loans.

posts.excerpt: How investors use 1031 exchanges to defer capital gains when trading up to higher-value property, and the deadlines that can't be missed.
posts.html:
A 1031 exchange lets a U.S. real estate investor defer capital gains tax by selling an investment property and reinvesting the proceeds in another "like-kind" investment property. The key rules: both properties must be held for investment or business use, you must identify replacement property within 45 days and close within 180 days, and a qualified intermediary must hold the funds.

Here are the basics for luxury investors. This is educational content, not tax advice.

Key takeaways

  • A 1031 exchange defers, but does not eliminate, capital gains tax.
  • It applies to investment and business property, not your primary residence.
  • Identify replacement property within 45 days of selling.
  • Complete the purchase within 180 days.
  • Use a qualified intermediary and a tax professional.

What is a 1031 exchange?

It's a provision in Section 1031 of the U.S. tax code that allows investors to defer capital gains tax when they exchange one investment property for another of like kind. In real estate, "like kind" is broad: most investment real estate can be exchanged for other investment real estate in the U.S.

Can you use a 1031 exchange for a luxury home?

Only if the property is held for investment or business use, such as a rental. A primary residence doesn't qualify. Vacation homes are a gray area with specific rules about personal use and rental history, so get professional advice.

What are the 1031 exchange deadlines?

Deadline Rule
45 days Identify potential replacement properties in writing
180 days Close on the replacement property

Both clocks start when you sell the original property and run at the same time. Missing either deadline can make the exchange fail.

What is a qualified intermediary?

A qualified intermediary is an independent party who holds the sale proceeds and uses them to buy the replacement property. If you receive the money yourself, the exchange can be disqualified.

Selling an investment property to trade up? A cinematic video helps it stand out and sell on schedule, which matters when deadlines are tight. Create My Free Video.

How do investors use 1031 exchanges to trade up?

Many investors use exchanges to move from smaller properties into higher-value ones, such as a portfolio of rentals into a luxury rental home or a property in a faster-growing market. To defer all of the gain, the replacement property generally needs to be of equal or greater value and use all the proceeds.

See our list of the best places to invest in luxury real estate.

What are common 1031 exchange mistakes?

  • Touching the sale proceeds instead of using an intermediary.
  • Missing the 45-day identification deadline.
  • Buying a replacement that's worth less, leaving taxable "boot."
  • Trying to exchange a primary residence.
  • Not planning the replacement purchase before selling.

Frequently asked questions

Does a 1031 exchange eliminate taxes?

No. It defers capital gains tax until you sell without exchanging. Tax planning can affect what happens later, so talk to a tax professional.

Can I exchange a rental for a vacation home?

It depends on how the vacation home is used. Personal use limits apply. Get advice before buying.

Can foreign investors use 1031 exchanges?

Rules can be more complex for foreign sellers, including FIRPTA withholding. See foreign buyers in Florida luxury real estate.

Do I need an attorney for a 1031 exchange?

You'll need a qualified intermediary, and a tax professional and real estate attorney are strongly recommended.

This article is for general information only and is not tax or legal advice. Consult a qualified tax professional before starting a 1031 exchange.

  • Loans above the limit are jumbo loans.
  • Lenders typically want strong credit, solid income documentation and cash reserves.
  • Down payment requirements vary by lender and loan size.
  • Shop several lenders, including private banks.

What is a jumbo loan?

A jumbo loan is a non-conforming mortgage: it's too large to meet the limits for loans backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Lenders keep these loans or sell them privately, so they set their own requirements.

What are the 2026 conforming loan limits?

2026 limit (one-unit homes) Amount
Baseline $832,750
High-cost area ceiling $1,249,125

The baseline rose by $26,250 from 2025. Limits vary by county, so check the figure for your area.

What do lenders require for a jumbo loan?

Requirements vary, but lenders commonly look at:

  • Credit score: usually stronger than for conforming loans.
  • Debt-to-income ratio: your monthly debts compared with income.
  • Down payment: often larger than for conforming loans.
  • Cash reserves: months of payments in savings or investments.
  • Documentation: tax returns, assets, sometimes two appraisals for very large loans.

How do jumbo loan rates compare?

Jumbo rates can be higher, similar or even lower than conforming rates depending on the market and lender. Private banks sometimes offer better terms to clients who hold assets with them. Compare offers from several lenders.

Should luxury buyers use a jumbo loan or pay cash?

Many luxury buyers pay cash, others finance to keep money invested elsewhere. The right choice depends on interest rates, returns on other investments, liquidity and taxes. Talk with your financial advisor.

How does jumbo financing affect the buying process?

Get pre-approved early. Sellers of high-end homes want proof you can close. Expect a more detailed underwriting process and a careful appraisal. See how to buy a luxury home.

What is the jumbo loan limit for 2026?

Any loan above the conforming limit is jumbo. For 2026, that's $832,750 in most areas and up to $1,249,125 in high-cost areas for one-unit homes.

How much down payment do I need for a jumbo loan?

It depends on the lender, loan size and your finances. Compare offers.

Can I get a jumbo loan for a second home or investment property?

Many lenders offer jumbo loans for second homes and investment properties, often with stricter requirements.

Are jumbo loans harder to get?

They usually have stricter requirements than conforming loans, but well-qualified buyers can find competitive options.

posts.meta: Second home or investment property? How the choice affects financing, taxes, rental rules and insurance for luxury buyers, explained in plain English.
posts.excerpt: The same house can be a second home or an investment property, and the label changes your loan, taxes and how you can use it.
posts.html:
The difference between a second home and an investment property comes down to how you use it. A second home is mainly for your own use, with limited or no rental. An investment property is bought to earn income or appreciation, usually through renting. The label affects your mortgage terms, taxes, insurance and what you're allowed to do with the home, so decide before you buy.

Here is how they compare. This is educational content, not financial or tax advice.

Key takeaways

  • Second homes are mainly for personal use. Investment properties are for income.
  • Lenders often offer better terms for second homes than for investment properties.
  • Tax treatment differs, especially for rental income and expenses.
  • Local short-term rental rules may limit how you can rent either one.
  • Be accurate with lenders and insurers about how you'll use the home.

What is the difference between a second home and an investment property?

Second home Investment property
Main purpose Personal use Income or appreciation
Renting Limited, if allowed Expected
Financing Often better terms Often stricter terms
Taxes Some owner deductions may apply Rental income and expenses reported
Insurance Homeowner or second-home policy Landlord or rental policy
1031 exchange Generally not eligible Can qualify

How does financing differ?

Lenders usually see second homes as lower risk than investment properties, so they may offer lower rates or smaller down payments. They typically require that you occupy the home for part of the year and limit how it's rented. Misrepresenting how you'll use a property on a loan application is a serious issue, so be accurate.

For larger loans, see jumbo loans explained.

How are taxes different?

Rental income from an investment property is generally taxable, and many related expenses may be deductible. Second homes have different rules, especially if you rent them for part of the year. Tax law is complex and changes, so talk to a tax professional.

Can you rent out a second home?

Sometimes, within limits set by your lender, insurer, HOA and local laws. Many cities restrict short-term rentals. See our guide to luxury vacation rental investment.

Which is better for luxury buyers?

It depends on your goals. If you want a place to spend time with family and possibly rent occasionally, a second home may fit. If your goal is income and long-term returns, an investment property structure makes more sense. Read our luxury real estate investing guide.

Frequently asked questions

Can a second home become an investment property later?

Yes, your use can change over time, but it may affect your loan terms, insurance and taxes. Check with your lender and advisors before changing how you use it.

Do second homes qualify for 1031 exchanges?

Generally, property held mainly for personal use doesn't qualify. See 1031 exchanges for luxury real estate.

Is insurance different for a rental property?

Yes. Rental properties typically need a landlord or short-term rental policy rather than a standard homeowner policy.

Which states are popular for luxury second homes?

Florida, Arizona, Nevada and resort areas across the country are popular. See best places to invest in luxury real estate.

posts.html:
Nine U.S. states don't tax wage income: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington and Wyoming. For high earners, that can mean big savings, which is one reason luxury demand has been strong in Florida, Nevada and Texas. Redfin's 2026 luxury reports point to buyers from New York and California moving to Florida partly for its favorable tax environment.

Here is what that means for luxury buyers and agents. This is educational content, not tax advice.

Key takeaways

  • Nine states don't tax wage income, including Florida, Texas, Nevada and Tennessee.
  • Tax savings are one reason high earners relocate, along with lifestyle and climate.
  • Florida luxury markets like Miami and Tampa led U.S. luxury price growth in 2026.
  • Property taxes, insurance and other costs still vary a lot. Look at the full picture.
  • Washington taxes certain capital gains, and New Hampshire's rules have changed over time, so check details.

Texas Austin, Dallas, Houston
Nevada Las Vegas, Lake Tahoe (Nevada side)
Tennessee Nashville

Wyoming Jackson Hole
South Dakota Limited luxury market
Alaska Limited luxury market
New Hampshire Seacoast and lakes region

How do income taxes affect luxury real estate demand?

For high earners and retirees with large incomes, state income tax can add up to a meaningful annual cost. Moving to a no-income-tax state can free up money, which some buyers put toward a home. Redfin's September 2026 report cited Florida's favorable tax environment, warm weather and waterfront lifestyle as draws for affluent buyers from New York and California.

Which no-income-tax markets are growing fastest?

In Redfin's data for the three months ending July 2026, Miami led the nation in luxury price growth (+18%), followed by Tampa (+15.4%), with Las Vegas fifth (+11.3%). See our reports on Miami, Tampa and Las Vegas.

What other costs should buyers compare?

No income tax doesn't mean low costs overall. Compare:

  • Property taxes, which can be high in some no-income-tax states.
  • Insurance, especially in coastal Florida and other storm-prone areas.
  • Sales taxes and other local taxes.
  • HOA fees and maintenance.

Our luxury investing guide covers carrying costs in detail.

Does moving states automatically change your tax residency?

No. Changing residency involves where you live, work and keep ties, and your former state may review it. Talk to a tax professional before you move.

Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington and Wyoming don't tax wage income. Washington taxes certain capital gains.

Why are wealthy buyers moving to Florida?

Common reasons include no state personal income tax, warm weather, waterfront living and a growing business scene, as noted in Redfin's 2026 reports.

Are property taxes higher in no-income-tax states?

Some, like Texas, have relatively high property taxes. Compare the total cost of ownership.

Do I pay federal taxes in a no-income-tax state?

Yes. Federal income tax applies everywhere in the U.S.

The luxury renovations that tend to add the most value improve how a home lives and photographs: updated kitchens, outdoor living spaces, primary suites, natural light and reliable systems. Highly personal choices, like bold finishes or niche rooms, often don't return their cost. Before any major project, compare it with what buyers in your price range expect.

Here is how to think about it. This is educational content, not financial advice.

Key takeaways

  • Focus on spaces buyers use and see most: kitchen, outdoor living, primary suite.
  • Fix systems and maintenance issues first. Buyers notice.
  • Avoid over-improving beyond what the neighborhood supports.
  • Neutral, quality finishes appeal to more buyers than bold personal choices.
  • Presentation can matter as much as renovation when selling.

Which renovations rarely pay off?

  • Niche rooms that few buyers want.
  • Expensive features that don't fit the neighborhood.

Over-improvement is spending more than the market will pay back, usually by renovating far beyond comparable homes nearby. A $2 million kitchen in a $3 million neighborhood rarely returns its cost. See how to value a luxury home.

Great presentation helps buyers see value. Professional photos, staging and cinematic video can make a well-kept home feel fresh without major construction. Combine smart updates with strong marketing for the best result.
